Amaravati.x: Amaravati or Amaravathi is the capital of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh, on the banks of the Krishna River, opposite Vijayawada (Bezawada) and northeast of Guntur. Nonetheless, Amaravati, Guntur and Vijayawada together constitute the Capital Region (CR) of Andhra Pradesh, the modern heart of the state since 2014.

Bhubaneswar.x: Bhubaneswar, the capital of Odisha, lies on the banks of the River Kuakhai which is part of the Mahanadi River delta. Together with Konark and Puri, it forms the Swarna Tribhuja or Golden Triangle of Odisha tourism. Haryana.x: Haryana is a state in northwestern India, southeast of Punjab. Often overlooked by the travellers to northern India, Haryana is home to various historical and religious sites. Hassan.x: Hassan is a small town in Karnataka State. It is a once-in-a-lifetime trip to the heart of Karnataka architecture, greenery and water.

Jaigaon.x: Jaigaon is a city in the Alipurduar district of West Bengal, India. It is a trading post for cross-border business with Bhutan. Unless you are planning to enter Bhutan or have an interest in construction material and fake branded clothes, there is no reason to visit Jaigaon.

Jharkhand.x: Jharkhand is a state in Eastern India. Home to the Chota Nagpur Plateau, Jharkhand can fairly claim to be one of the most attractive parts of the country. The scenery of the main plateau is most attractive with its undulations, detached abrupt hills and forest tracts.

Patna.x: Patna, the capital of Bihar, is a bustling city in the Indian Plains with a glorious past. It is a gateway to the Buddhist and Jain pilgrimage centres of Vaishali, Rajgir, Nalanda, Bodh Gaya, Kesariya and Pawapuri.

Hosur.x: Hosur is an industrial town in northern Tamil Nadu, on the bank of the River Ponnaiyar. It is considered the manufacturing twin of Bangalore (Bengaluru) due to its presence of major manufacturing industries, compared to Bangalore's presence of major IT industries.

It is a very picturesque city with splendid palaces, forts and historical monuments and belongs to the tourist Golden Triangle along with Delhi and Agra.

Jammu.x: Jammu, the largest city in the Jammu region of northern India, is the winter capital of Jammu and Kashmir, sitting at a low elevation in the mainly mountainous state. Srinagar, the state's summer capital, is at a much higher elevation.

Jamnagar.x: Jamnagar, the Jewel of Kathiawar, is a coastal city on the Gulf of Kutch, in the state of Gujarat, India. Ichalkaranji has experienced rapid industrial growth since the mid‑20th century, evolving from a small princely town into a major economic hub with strong cooperative and entrepreneurial traditions.

Jaunpur.x: Jaunpur is a city in the Purvanchal part of Eastern Uttar Pradesh. A historical town with Medieval era fort, bridges and mosques. The city was founded by Feroz Shah Tughlaq and named in memory of his cousin, Jaun (popularly known as Muhammad bin Tughluq).

sights.img: Thomas Daniell - View of the Fort, Jaunpur, Uttar Pradesh.jpg

sights.d: A picturesque 16th century bridge across the Gombti which was constructed during Mughal times.
The mosque was constructed in 1408 by Ibrahim Shah Sharki. The foundation stone of the mosque was laid by Feorze Shah Tughlaque in 1393.
Built by Hussain Shah Sharqi, the 15th century is one of the largest in India.
sights.img: Main arcade facade, Jama Masjid, Jaunpur.jpg

sights.d: This small mosque is a hidden gem. It is located deep inside the Mufti Mohalla locality of Jaunpur and is difficult to find.

Feroz Shah (not to be confused with Feroz Shah Tughlaq) was a commander of Babur. The tomb consists of a single domed structure.

Jhansi.x: Jhansi is a city in the Northern Bundelkhand region of Uttar Pradesh, India. It is very close to the central state of Madhya Pradesh and is overall more similar culturally to much of Madhya Pradesh than the rest of Uttar Pradesh. Jhansi's claim to fame is being the city where Rani Lakshmibai resisted against the British in the Great Rebellion of 1857.
Jhansi.icon: View of Jhansi from Sipri's Hilltop.jpg

sights.d: The fort of Jhansi was built in 1613, by Raja Bir Singh Judao (1606-27) of Orchha. This fort is built on a rocky hill and the city of Jhansi is around this fort.
sights.img: Inside the Rani Laxmibai's Jhansi Fort in Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh 04.jpg

sights.d: Rani Mahal was built by Raghunath II of Newalkar family (1769-96). Rani Mahal is decorated with multicoloured paintings and art forms.
Baruasagar is around 24 km from Jhansi. It is a small town on the bank of Betwa river. It has a large lake which is called Barua sagar tal.
Chirgaon is 30 km from Jhansi, It is on the banks of Betwa river. It is on National Highway 25.
The Government Museum is in a very picturesque location in the heart of the city. The surrounding area has some beautiful parks.
This temple is in Jhansi cantonment. The beauty of this place is to visit it during sunrise.

Jhargram.x: Jhargram is a town in the southwest region of West Bengal, India.

sights.d: The zoo houses deer, snakes, peacocks, bears, crocodiles, black rabbits and various types of monkeys.
350 year old temple.

Jharsuguda.x: Jharsuguda is an upcoming industrial hub, popularly known as the powerhouse of Odisha, due to the large aluminium and power plants accessible from the city. Jharsuguda is located at the western end of Odisha (formerly known as Orissa).

Jind.x: Jind is a city in Haryana.

Jodhpur.x: Jodhpur is the second largest city in the state of Rajasthan. It is called the Gateway to Thar, as it is on the edge of the Thar desert. It is also called the Sun City as the sun shines (bright and hot) almost every day of the year.

sights.d: Dominates the city and is the largest fort in all Rajasthan. Founded in 1458 as the site of Rao Jodha's new capital — hence the name, Jodhpur — the city has…

Jorhat.x: Jorhat is a city of about 150,000 people (as of 2011) in Assam. It was the capital of the Ahom Kingdom.

sights.d: Hoollongapar Gibbon Sanctuary is an isolated protected area of evergreen forest located near Mariani in Jorhat district. The sanctuary is famous for the Hoolock gibbons.

Junagadh.x: Junagadh is a historical city in Gujarat, in the west of India, on the Arabian Sea. The region of Junagadh became a district of Gujarat state in 1960. Junagadh used to be the state capital and is now a district administrative center.

Kakinada.x: Kakinada is a port city in central Andhra Pradesh, and a part of the mighty River Godavari Delta Region.

KGF.x: KGF (Kolar Gold Fields) is a town in the Kolar district of Karnataka.

Murshidabad.x: Murshidabad is a historic town in central West Bengal. It was the capital of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha during the Nawab rule. The last capital city of independent Bengal was named after Nawab Murshid Quli Khan, the Diwan of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha.

Rayalaseema.x: Rayalaseema, the western region of Andhra Pradesh, covers the undulating landscapes of the Deccan Plateau, in contrast to Coastal Andhra. The two regions are separated by the Eastern Ghats.

Kaithal.x: Kaithal is a city in Ambala Division of Haryana to the north of Delhi. The area is mostly farmland, growing rice, cotton and oil-seed. Kaithal's sights include the fort and the Shree Gyarah Rudri Mandir Temple.

sights.d: Purported to be the place where the only female ruler of the Delhi Sultanate was originally buried.
The resting place of the 16th century Islamic saint.

Janjgir.x: Janjgir is the headquarters of Janjgir-Champa district in the Indian state of Chhattisgarh.

Jiaganj.x: Jiaganj or Ziaganj, a heritage town in Murshidabad, is popularised by former playback singer Arijit Singh, who was born here.

This is an important pilgrimage center since it is the birthplace of Sri Adi Sankara, one of India's foremost philosopher saints who preached the monistic or 'Advaita' philosophy.

Kallooppara.x: Kallooppara is a village in Central Travancore in India. Kallooppara is on the eastern side of Thiruvalla. This pilgrim center is at the central part of the blue waters of the Manimala River.

Kalyani.x: Kalyani is a planned township in the Nadia district of West Bengal, India.

Kanchipuram.x: Kanchipuram or Kancheepuram, formerly Conjeevaram, is a major pilgrimage site in northern Tamil Nadu. One of the most important spiritual centres of Hinduism, Kanchipuram has several medieval temples with spectacular architecture. It used to be the capital of the Pallava kingdom from the 4th to the 10th century, and was a centre of learning for all the major religions of South India.

sights.d: The highest, largest and most impressive temple in town, spanning 40 acres and dating back to the Pallava period.
Abode of Kamakshi (Parvati), consort of Shiva.

Kangra.x: Kangra is a town in Himachal Pradesh.

North 24 Parganas.x: North 24 Parganas, the most populous district of West Bengal, is also one of the state's most diverse districts, from the sprawling suburbs along the Hooghly River to the rural borderlands along the Ichamati River. The district borders Nadia to the north, Bangladesh to the east, Kolkata and South 24 Parganas to the south, and Hooghly and Howrah to the west.

Santiniketan.x: Santiniketan or Shantiniketan is a university town in central West Bengal, where students of different backgrounds study in open air, under the canopy of a tree. It is deeply associated with the Bengali poet Rabindranath Tagore who developed the town. It is considered the manifestation of a utopian ideal of a community that became a crucible for intellectual and artistic ideas that were to have a decisive impact on 20th-century art, literature, poetry, music and architecture in South Asia.

sights.d: Prayer place (under the chātim tree) of Maharshi Debendranath Tagore, father of Rabindranath Tagore.

sights.d: College of fine arts and crafts, has a museum exhibiting sculptures, frescoes and murals and a library of art books.
Secondary school, is of particular interest, being an example of the traditional gurukula method of learning, although things have changed slightly.

Thane.x: Thane, formerly known as Thana, is a city in North Konkan, Maharashtra. Its biggest claim to fame is that the first railway line laid in India was from Bori Bunder to Thane station.

sights.d: The lake is home to a small island with a Shiv temple on it and also a Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Statue behind it.
It is one of the oldest temples in Thane. It was reconstructed by Chimajji Appa around 1750 AD.

Kalaburagi.x: Kalaburagi, previously known as Gulbarga, is a city in Northern Karnataka and the head quarters of the Kalaburagi District. Gulburga literally means "city of gardens" while Kaliburagi means "rocky land." It was once the capital of the Bahmani Sultanate and an important Sufi centre.

sights.d: The fort dates back to the time of the Kakatiya dynasty. Later, the fort was turned into a mighty citadel under the Bahmani Sultanate.
A group of tombs of the Bahmani dynasty built during the 14th and 15th centuries. The tombs are examples of early Indo-Islamic architecture.
Banda Nawaz was a Sufi saint of Chishti Order. He was invited by the Bahmini Sultan Firoz Shah to settle in Gulbaraga (Kalaburagi) in 1399/1400.
sights.img: Main Shrine, Hazrath Khwaja Bande Nawaz, Gulbarga.jpg

sights.d: This single-domed structure stands on the north-western corner of the citadel next to the fort walls. The structure probably doubled up as a watch tower.
The temple houses the Samadhi of Sharana Basaveshwara, a 12th century Indian philosopher, poet, Lingayat social reformer of bhakti movement.

Kalka.x: Kalka is in Haryana, right up at the northeastern tip of the state on the border with Himachal Pradesh.

sights.d: Mughal style garden with seven terraces. A museum is also located here.

Kanhangad.x: Kanhangad or Hosdurg is a city in the Kasaragod district of the Malabar region of Kerala, India.

sights.d: Daily lecture sessions from 3:30PM to 4:30PM. Free food and accommodation to all visitors. Gardens, Bhajan Hall, Goshalas and Library.

Kannauj.x: Kannauj is a town on the Ganges in western Uttar Pradesh.

Kanchrapara.x: Kanchrapara is a railway town in the North 24 Parganas district of West Bengal.

Kamptee.x: Kamptee is a cantonment town near Nagpur in India, near the confluence of the Kanhan, Pench and Kolar rivers.

Kanyakumari.x: Kanyakumari or Kanniyakumari is a town on the southernmost tip of the mainland of India, in the state of Tamil Nadu. It is also known as Cape Comorin.

sights.d: The Rock has two Mandaps (halls); one belonging to Swami Vivekananda and the other belonging to a Holy Foot.
Thiruvalluvar Statue is dedicated to arguably the greatest Tamil poet, philosopher and saint, Thiruvalluvar.
On the shoreline of the Bay of Bengal, the 100-year-old Church of Our Lady of Ransom is dedicated to Mother Mary.
A fort on the shores of the Bay of Bengal, constructed in the 16th century by the Portuguese. The view of the sea line and coast from the fort is marvellous.
Vivekanandapuram is the headquarters of the Vivekananda Kendra and the centre spreads over an area of 100 acres. There is a well stocked library within the premises.
Kanyakumari Devi Temple is the main reason for naming the place as Kannyakumari or the "Land of the unmarried girl". This temple is close to the beach.

Kannur.x: Kannur, formerly Cannanore, is a seaside city on the northern side of Kerala (Keralam), India. The Aralam Wildlife Sanctuary on the Western Ghats is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Kannur (old name Cannanore) is known as Land of Looms and Lore because of the importance of the fabric industry and the concentration of Theyyam temple dance festivals.

Kanpur.x: Kanpur is the largest city in the state of Uttar Pradesh, India. It was known as Cawnpore in colonial times and is a major industrial centre of the Plains. The city is famous for its chemical (fertiliser, detergent), textile, and leather industries.
Kanpur.icon: JK Temple(Juggilal Kamlapati temple) is a temple in the Indian city of Kanpur.It is considered to be a unique blend of ancient and modern architecture.jpg

Kappad.x: Kappad, or Kappakadavu locally, is famous as the beach near Calicut, India, where the Portuguese explorer Vasco Da Gama landed on May 20, 1498. A small stone monument there commemorates the landing with the inscription, "Vasco da Gama landed here, Kappakadavu, in the year 1498." It is one of the most important tourist places in Kerala, with a wide and beautiful beach.

Kappil.x: Kappil is a town in Kerala, India. It is on the border between Thiruvananthapuram District and Kollam Districts, and five kilometers from the famous Varkala beach.

Kapurthala.x: Kapurthala is a small town in the state of Punjab in India.

sights.d: Once home of Maharaja Jagatjit Singh, it is the most impressive building in the city, inspired by European palaces. Built in 1906. Today it houses a school.

Karaikal.x: Karaikal district, part of the discontiguous union territory of Pondicherry, is a small enclave within Tamil Nadu. Karaikal and the other parts of Pondicherry are former French colonial territories in India. Karaikal district has a population of 200,000 and the main town is also called Karaikal.

Karjat.x: Karjat is a village in Maharastra. The river Ulhas originates in Karjat and flows westward. If you want to visit Karjat then the rainy season is best for you as Karjat has got such wonderful & beautiful waterfalls.

Karnal.x: Karnal is a city of 287,000 people (2011) in the National Capital Region (NCR) in Haryana. The city associates itself with Karna, the great donor and warrior and of one of the major characters of the Hindu epic Mahābhārata. The city has built a large statue in his honour.

sights.d: Well maintained park with gardens and fountains. Travelers and local populace enjoy this park for picnics and leisurely strolls.

Karnala Bird Sanctuary.x: Karnala Bird Sanctuary is a protected wildlife park in the Raigad district of Maharashtra, around 50 km from Mumbai. It is a major attraction to the visitors of Mumbai, Thane and other nearby towns. About 100,000 domestic tourists visit the sanctuary every year.

sights.d: Apart from being a place of interest to the naturalist, Karnala is redolent of martial history.

Karur.x: Karur is a town of some 10,76,588 (2011 census) people in Central Tamil Nadu.

Karwar.x: Karwar is a city in Karnataka.

Kasaragod.x: Kasaragod is a city in Kasaragod District at the northern end of Malabar, Kerala in India.

Kasauli.x: Kasauli is a small town in the state of Southern Himachal Pradesh located at an altitude of 1,927 m. The town is 77 km from Shimla and 70 km from Chandigarh.

sights.d: Close to the bus stand, it was constructed by the British family that founded the town of Kasauli itself. It is a magnificent structure built in the shape of a cross.

Kashmir Valley.x: The Kashmir Valley, or more poetically the Vale of Kashmir, is a large valley in the Himalayas and a part of Jammu and Kashmir in northern India.

Udupi.x: Most Indians know of Udupi not as a place, but as a category of restaurants that serve vegetarian food in the South Indian style. However, the town itself is not as well-known as its widespread cuisine. Still fewer know of its reputation as the location of a Krishna temple and a monastery established by the founder of one of the three main philosophical strains of present-day Hinduism.

sights.d: A complex of temples and monasteries located near the Madhva Sarovara, or Madhvacharya's pond.
sights.img: Udupi Sri Krishna Temple, Udupi, Karnataka, India (2007).jpg

sights.d: This is a temple dedicated to Parashurama, another incarnation of Vishnu, and according to legend, the creator of the landmass encompassing Udupi, Dakshina Kannada and…
The unusual feature of Udupi's Krishna temple is that the statue faces west, and away from the devotees.
Madhva Sarovara is right next to the temple and is accessible from both inside and outside of it.
Right next to the Krishna temple is this temple dedicated to Shiva, to whom, according to legend, the moon (Chandra) prayed at this spot.
Visit Malpe beach where you can take fantastic pictures of the sunset in the background of St Mary's island. Nice clean beach, not inundated by tourists.

Katihar.x: Katihar is a city in the north eastern part of the Indian state of Bihar. The city is somewhat close to the Nepalese border and is also the capital of the Katihar district.

sights.d: One of the largest wetland and bird watching areas in the state. In 2019, it became Bihar's first conservation reserve.

Karmatanr.x: Karmatanr is a hamlet in the Santhal Parganas region of Jharkhand, associated with the later life of Bengali writer Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.

sights.d: The residence of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar in Karmatanr. His house is converted into a museum named "Vidyasagar Smriti", which contains a collection of his personal…

Kathgola.x: Kathgola is a small town north of Murshidabad, on the eastern bank of the Bhagirathi River, famous for the Kathgola Palace and the Jagat Seths.

sights.d: Once the residence of the Dugar family, now a museum showcasing chandeliers, mirrors, furniture and other artefacts.
The Jagat Seths were a business family and were involved in the business of banking and money lending.
sights.img: House Of Jagat Seth Complex - Mahimapur - Murshidabad 2017-03-28 6165-6169.tif

sights.d: About half a mile from the Hazarduari Palace is Jafarganj Cemetery. The Cemetery contains the tombs of the Nawab's Nazim, from Mir Jafar to Humayun Jah.
Nimak Haram Deorhi is the gateway to Mir Jafars palace. The palace lo longer exist but the entrance gate still stands.
Azimunnisa Begum, was the daughter of Murshid Quli Khan. According to legend she was diagnosed with an incurable disease.
Though some of its early glory has been lost, the temple remains a major tourist attraction, chiefly because of the beautiful temple with an admirable work of stucco.

Karnasuvarna.x: Karnasuvarna, an archaeological site in Murshidabad, covers the ruins of the former capital of Bengal under Shashanka.
Karnasuvarna.icon: Raja Karna's Palace alias Karnasubarna at Murshidabad district in West Bengal.jpg

sights.d: Ruins of a Buddhist university.

Katra.x: Katra, also known as Katra Vaishno Devi, is a city in the Reasi district of the union territory of Jammu and Kashmir administered by India. It is in the foothills of the Trikuta Mountains, about 42 km from the city of Jammu, and 35 km from Udhampur. The main attraction is the Maa Vaishno Devi temple.

sights.d: The temple is home to a famous Hindu goddess. The temple is on a mountain, with a climb of 12 km to reach it.

Kavali.x: Kavali is a city in southern Andhra Pradesh in India.

sights.d: one of famous temple in kavali geetamandram its located in railway station road kavali
don't miss seeing this temple

Kavalkinaru.x: Kavalkinaru is a beautiful village in the state of Tamil Nadu. Here, all religious people live together as one family. The village is a 45 Min drive from Thirunelveli and a 30 min drive from Nagercoil, and has a well connected road network and rail network.

Kayamkulam.x: Kayamkulam is a city and a municipality in district of the Indian state of Kerala. It is an ancient maritime trading centre and is almost equidistant from Alappuzha town and Kollam.
Kayamkulam.banner: Azheekkal Bridge view from Harbor 2022 June (cropped).jpg

sights.d: Palace and museum with exhibits about the Travancore kingdom. The palace was built during the 18th century by Travancore Maharaja Marthanda Varma.

Keoladeo Bird Sanctuary.x: The Keoladeo Bird Sanctuary, otherwise known as the Keoladeo Ghana National Park and originally called Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary, is one of the world's most renowned bird feeding and breeding grounds. The park is over 29 km² and has 364 species of birds, including some threatened migratory birds from central Asia. It is also a major tourist centre with scores of ornithologists arriving here in the hibernal season.
Keoladeo Bird Sanctuary.icon: Keoladeo Ghana National Park, Bharatpur, Rajasthan, India.jpg

sights.d: The sanctuary is named after this 300-year-old Shiva temple, which is within the national park. It has a peaceful and serene atmosphere.

Keonjhar.x: Keonjhar, officially Kendujhar, is the district headquarter of Keonjhar District in Odisha (formerly Orissa).
Keonjhar.icon: KEONJHAR town as seen from above..jpg

sights.d: waterfall
A small but very beautiful waterfall.
The largest temple.
You may go by bus or by reservation. The bus fare is ₹20 from Anandpur and ₹110 from Bhubaneswar.
Dedicated to Lord Shiva.

Khajuraho.x: Khajuraho, a small town in the Bundelkhand region of Eastern Madhya Pradesh, is famous for groups of Hindu and Jain temples. These temples are a UNESCO World Heritage Site for their beautiful and erotic rock carvings. Khajuraho has the Vindhya range of mountains as its beautiful backdrop.

sights.d: This is the only granite temple in the Khajuraho group.
It is dedicated to Lord Chitragupta, the bookkeeper of the good and bad deeds.
Dedicated to the Goddess (devi), this is smaller and much more delicately proportioned temple and is home to some of the finest sculptures of Khajuraho.
This temple is decorated with a profusion of sculptures that are among the greatest masterpieces of Indian art.
The oldest and finest of the western group of temples, named after the ruler that built the temple.
A temple dedicated to Shiva, a huge 8ft Lingam adorns the temple.

Khammam.x: Khammam is in the Telangana state of Southern India. It gets its name from "stambhadri" which became "kambham" and the British Raj used to call the place "Khammam Mettu". The municipal corporation offers the small town experience with easy accessibility to modern amenities and entertainment.

sights.d: This fort was built by Kakatiya rulers and was managed and extended by Nizam. It offers a nice view of Khammam town. There are steps constructed to facilitate climbing.
This temple of the "Narasimha Swami" deity is quite famous and also the reason for the name of "Khammam". On a hill top, it offers nice views especially in the evenings.
Danavaigudem Park is a picnic spot on the banks of Munneru river. You can check out the drinking water supply plant here, and you could also have a nice walk crossing…
An evening at Tankbund near sequel resorts is a good pastime.This place is also used as walkers park in the morning.

Kinnigoli.x: Kinnigoli is a city of 17,000 people (2011) in Dakshina Kannada. It is a major suburb in the outskirts of Mangalore Tehsil (Mangalore Township) about 32 km from Mangalore City.

Lonavla.x: Lonavla or Lonavala is in the Pune district of Maharashtra, India.

sights.d: A waterfall near the dam is a popular spot between Lonavla and I.N.S. Shivaji. Buses running on the I.N.S. Shivaji Road stop here.
Karla, near Lonavla, is a complex of cave shrines built by Buddhist monks around 3rd to 2nd century BC.
Another point in the town of Lonavla is the wax museum founded by Sunil Kandaloor, a 37-year-old wax artist from Kerala.
Duke's Nose stands 12 km from Lonavla, clearly visible from the highway while driving towards Mumbai. This landmark in Khandala is popular with hikers.
A naval engineer training base.
Lonavla Lake is surrounded by natural scenery, about 1.6 km from the town. The lake dries up during the winter months.

Khambhat.x: Khambhat (formerly Cambay) is in Gujarat, in Anand District at the inland end of the Gulf of Khambhat.

sights.d: The 14th-century mosque is built with peculiar archaeological designs and structures borrowed from the Jain temples built at that time.
Visit this only after checking the tidal information for the seashore, as the gulf has pretty much silted up.
which submerges on a high tide day.
for a picturesque view of palm trees adorning the road.
comprises shrines of all deities and a Nataraj artifact made out of stone.
A historical stepwell is located on an island in the lake. The lake is surrounded by a walkway and has children's play area.

Khopoli.x: Khopoli is an industrial town of 109,000 people (2011) in the Raigad district of Maharashtra, at the base of the Sahyadri mountains. Patalganga River flows through Khopoli. The city is called a city of waterfalls due to the number of waterfalls in the rainy season.

sights.d: A mountain pass between Khopoli and Khandala on the crest of the Western Ghats.
India's largest theme park. It is split into six zones: Viva Europa, Americana, Jambo Africa, Asiana, Arabia and India.
It has a Parashurama temple and Fire temple or Agni Mandir which was built in 1971.

Kavalande.x: Kavalande is a village near Nanjangud town in Mysore of Karnataka state, India.

Khurja.x: Khurja is a city (and a municipal board) in the Bulandshahr district in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh. It is situated around 85 km from Delhi.

Katwa.x: Katwa is a town in the Purba Bardhaman district of West Bengal, at the southern bank of the Ajay River.
Katwa.banner: Aatchala temple of Chandra family at Bagtikra under Katwa police station in Purba Bardhaman district 11 (cropped).jpg

sights.img: Tomb of William Carrey Junior at Katwa 06.jpg

sights.d: A green park with scenic views of the Ajay River.
A temple complex near Sri Gauranga Bari. It consists of the principle Kali temple, along with the temples of Lord Shiva, Lord Vishnu and Durga.
In January 1510, Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu received diksha from his guru Keshab Bharati at the site of the current Sri Gauranga Bari Temple in Katwa.

Kharagpur.x: Kharagpur, the largest city in Southwest Bengal, is a major railway, industrial and academic hub of West Bengal.
Kharagpur.icon: Kharagpur Railway Junction Station - Kharagpur - West Midnapore 2013-01-26 3621.JPG

sights.d: A park and a picnic spot, frequented by people of all ages. It offers toy train rides within the park.
Built by the British for the Royal Indian Air Force during World War II.
The first Indian Institute of Technology, established in 1951. The IIT attracts visitors throughout the year (especially in the spring academic semester from January to…
IIT Kharagpur was originally a detention camp during the British Raj to imprison Indian independence activists.
sights.img: Hijli Detention Camp Converted Hijli Shaheed Bhavan - IIT Kharagpur - West Midnapore 2015-09-28 4768.JPG

sights.d: The temple was established in the early 20th century by some Bengali people working on the railways. It is famous for its Durga Puja and is very popular.
It’s a famous picnic spot in winter. There is a small deer park inside.

Khadikolvan.x: Khadikolvan is a historic and culturally significant village in the Sangameshwar Taluka of Ratnagiri district, South Konkan, Maharashtra, India. The village is known for its traditional temples, hot springs, and proximity to the famous Marleshwar Temple.

Khardaha.x: Khardaha or Khardah is a temple town in the North 24 Parganas district of West Bengal. It is a pilgrimage site of the Vaishnava denomination of Hinduism.

sights.d: A riverside at-chala temple complex built between late 18th century and early 19th century by zamindars Ramhari Biswas and Ramkrishna Biswas.

sights.img: Gopinath temple at Khardaha in North 24 Parganas district, West Bengal 01.jpg

sights.d: Nityananda Mahaprabhu chose this building for kirtan at the order of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.
sights.img: Kunjabati Premises at Khardaha in North 24 Pargana district, West Bengal 02.jpg

sights.d: A nine-pinnacled (navaratna) temple housing the idols of Jagannath, Chaitanya and Nityananda, three Mahaprabhus of Gaudiya Vaishnavism.
sights.img: Mahaprabhu Temple at Khardaha in North 24 Parganas district, West Bengal 04.jpg

sights.d: A holy place associated with Ramakrishna and Swami Vivekananda. It is decorated with colorful light, kadamba flower made of sola and birds during the Ras festival.
sights.img: Rashkhola Rashmancha at Khardaha in North 24 Parganas district, West Bengal 07.jpg

sights.d: A temple established by Birbhadra Goswami, son of Nityananda Mahaprabhu. Birbhadra was born in 1457 at Kunjabati.
sights.img: Radha Shyamsundar Jiu temple at Khardaha in North 24 Parganas district, West Bengal 06.jpg

Katni.x: Katni is a city in Eastern Madhya Pradesh.

sights.d: A historic 19th-century fort that became a prominent hotspot during the 1857 Rebellion.
The geographic centre of modern post-partition India is marked by a replica of an Ashokan Pillar.
An over-100-ft waterfall surrounded by jungle.

Kodikunnu.x: Kodikunnu is in Central Kerala, India.

Kolhapur.x: Kolhapur is a city in the south west of Maharashtra. It has a population of around 619,000. It is situated on the banks of river Panchganga and is famous for the Mahalakshmi Temple as a pilgrimage city and is also famous for having 2 sites that are UNESCO World Heritage Sites, namely, the Panhala Fort and the Radhanagari Wildlife Sanctuary.

sights.d: Built in 1100 AC. Historic memories of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. Hill Station. Carrying a rich heritage, Panhala Fort forms the largest of all the Deccan forts.
sights.img: Baji Prabhu Deshpande Statue in Panhala Fort.jpg

sights.d: The puranas have listed 108 sites where Shakti (the goddess of power) is manifested.
Residence and a museum about memories of The Great Lokraja Shahuji Maharaj.
A gateway of higher education of international level to regional masses but surrounded by rich nature.
Temblai hill is a famous spot in Kolhapur. There is a temple of Goddess "Temlabai" and other small temple on this Hill.
Beautiful rainy hill station, lot of clouds and beautiful waterfall.

Kolkata.x: Kolkata, formerly and still fondly called Calcutta, is the largest city in eastern India and the capital of the state of West Bengal. Once the capital of the British Raj till 1911, Kolkata is said to have been built on three villages along the Hooghly River, a distributary of the mighty Ganges. The city has seen tremendous growth during and after the partition of India in 1947.

Kollam.x: Kollam, previously Quilon, is a city in southern Kerala (Keralam), India. West and slightly north of the town some 5 km (3.1 mi) lies a beach, on the north end of which are various European colonial-era relics, including the ruins of a fort and a few churches. There are also some old colonial buildings scattered about the town.

sights.d: A vestige of the Portuguese rule of Kollam, established in 1614.
Some limited standing ruins of an old colonial fort. You can see two different sides of the building, the first from the harbour side (where it is visible at some…
A modern lighthouse in a historic Christian quarter that is possible to climb in the afternoons.
Scenic place, with blue green stretches back water, coconut palms, back water cruise, house boats, Ayurvedic treatment centers.
Pilgrim centre, old trade route for merchants from either sides of western Ghats, famous for shrine of Lord Sastha, fine sculptures and mural paintings.

Konkan.x: Konkan is a coastal region of Western India, consisting of the coastal areas of Maharashtra and Goa. Some definitions include the entire western coast of India, from Gujarat to Kerala.
Konkan.icon: Deogad Beach in Sindhudurg district ,Konkan region Maharashtra, India.JPG

Koraput.x: Koraput is a city in the state of Odisha, near the borders of Andhra Pradesh and Chhattisgarh states. It has enchanting hills, verdant forests, winding streams, exotic wildlife and a rich tribal way of life.
Koraput.icon: Deomali by Santanu Mahapatra, Koraput - panoramio.jpg

sights.d: It is across the Kolab River, 900 m (3,000 feet) above sea level with facilities for hydroelectricity generation.
River Kolab forms three waterfalls of about 9 m (30 feet). The last 5 km of the road from Khandaguda is 'kutcha road' (dirt track). There is a rest house near the falls.
The highest & largest mountain peak of Odisha.
The Machkunda River forms the 175 m high waterfalls, with facilities for generation of hydroelectricity at Machkunda Power Station.
Cave shrine of Lord Shiva on the banks of the River Shabari. The place name literally means 'hidden God'. Odisha Tourism has a lodge at Gupteswar.

Koravangala.x: Koravangala in Karnataka has the Buchishwara temple built by Hoyasalas. The temple is in good condition.

sights.img: Koravangala Shri Bucheswara Temple - Front Side.jpg

Korba.x: Korba is a city in Chhattisgarh. Korba is the power capital of Chhattisgarh. The district comes under Bilaspur division and is inhabited mainly by tribals including the protected tribe Korwas (Pahadi Korwa).

sights.d: It was constructed by Raja Pratwidev First. Archeologists consider it as one of the strongest natural fort.

Kota.x: Kota is in the Hadoti region of Rajasthan, which is in the southeastern side of the state. The Chambal river flows through the town, because of which the city of Kota is unlike the arid climate prevalent in the state.

sights.d: (25 km) An archeological area with ancient Indian stone carvings.
This garden stretches along the banks of the river Chambal. It houses a pond with rare gharial and crocodiles, which can be crossed via a teetering suspension bridge.
(50 km) - One of 3 wildlife sanctuaries in Rajasthan with large tracts of forests and a variety of wildlife
Palace and fort complex often visited by tourists.
It is a Hanuman temple at few km from Chambal garden.
Right in the center of the artificial Kishore Sagar tank (Lake Pichola) stands the beautiful red sandstone monument, Jagmandir.

Kottayam.x: Kottayam is a city in Kerala, south India. It is near to Kochi. The city is India's first 100% literate city, also known as Letter Capital of Kerala, due to headquarters of more than a dozen publishing houses and newspaper companies as well as several famous colleges and university.

sights.d: A hill station with large hills around high. Beautiful hillocks named Mankunnu, Kudayathoormala, Thonippara and Poonchira are here.
Important pilgrimage centre for Hindus and Muslims.
Famous for having an ancient Shiva temple. Wall paintings in the temple are thousands of years old.
The place is famous for its bird sanctuary, house boats, backwaters, canals and the bungalow of Henry Baker (now run as part of a resort managed by the Taj group of…
St. Mary's Shrine here attracts people of all faiths. Various kinds of offerings are made here devotees.
This is a small white sand island. It gets its name from the brilliant reflection of moonlight from the sand.

Kovalam.x: Kovalam, a fishing village in southern Kerala, is famous for its beaches, among the most pristine in India. About 17 km (11 mi) from Thiruvananthapuram, Kovalam is extremely popular among westerners due to shallow waters and low tidal waves. This article also covers the nearby Vizhinjam, which is best known for the international seaport and the tidal power station.

sights.d: The granite cave encloses a one-celled shrine with a loose sculpture of Vinadhara Dakshinamurthi.
sights.img: Rock cut cave - Vizhinjam, Kerala, India.jpg

sights.d: The old lighthouse, at the southern beach is a local landmark, for being one of the oldest lighthouses of Kerala, guiding ships to the nearby Vizhnjam port.
The Tamil-style koil is known for the tall Gangadhareshwara sculpture, the tallest Shiva sculpture in Kerala.
Head down to the harbour at sunset for some spectacular shots of the area with the seaside mosque in the background.
The largest and southernmost beach of Kovalam, known for its 35-m-high lighthouse which towers over it atop Kurumkal hillock.
The second-largest beach of Kovala, and it takes less than five minutes to walk from Lighthouse Beach.

Kovilpatti.x: Kovilpatti is a city in Thoothukudi District of Tamil Nadu. It's nicknamed as "City of Matches".

Kongu Nadu.x: Kongu Nadu in western Tamil Nadu consists of 10 districts, namely Coimbatore, Dharmapuri, Dindigul, Erode, Karur, Krishnagiri, Namakkal, Nilgiris, Salem and Tiruppur.
Kongu Nadu.banner: WV banner Western Tamil Nadu Metupalayam panorama.jpg

Kotdwar.x: Kotdwar aka Kotdwara is a town in Garhwal district of Uttarakhand. It is one of the main gateways to Uttarakhand.

sights.d: Kanva Ashram is an important historical and archaeological place.
Approximately 2 km from Kotdwar, this renowned temple is dedicated to Lord Hanuman. Large numbers visit year round.

Konanur.x: Konanur (Paduvalamarahalli) is a village near Nanjangud in Mysore district of Karnataka state in India. .

Kotkapura.x: Kotkapura is a city of 92,000 people (2011) in Punjab (India). It is the largest city in the Faridkot District. Kot Kapura has also been called the 'City of White Gold' due to its cotton market, which was once the largest cotton market in Asia.

Kondapalli.x: Kondapalli is a village 16 km (9.9 mi) west of Vijayawada in central Andhra Pradesh. The village is known for making toys with light-weight wood sourced from the hill forest.

sights.d: Built on a hill, this fort features an impressive three-storeyed rock tower and was witness to the glory of many dynasties.
Spread over an area of , the forest is home to several carnivores like leopards, wild dogs, and a few others like, jackals, wolves and civet cats.

Kolaghat.x: Kolaghat is a popular picnic spot in the Purba Medinipur district of West Bengal, along the Rupnarayan River.

Kishangarh.x: Kishangarh is a town near Ajmer, in central Rajasthan. Founded in 1609-1611 by Kishan Singh, the town is home to the Rathore clan of the Rajputs, as well as the marble slurry dumping yard turned into a snow-themed park.

sights.d: This former waste disposal site for marble processing byproducts is now a snow-themed park by the Kishangarh Marble Association (KMA).

Kozhikode.x: Kozhikode, formerly Calicut, is the second-largest city in the Indian state of Kerala (Keralam) after Kochi.

sights.d: 7 mangrove species, 29 mangrove associates and fauna ranging from protozoa to Otter. It is also a congenial habitat for 20 types of water birds.
Ideal place for students of Indian history.
Copies of megalithic monuments.
600-year-old structure. Beautiful pond surrounded by several old buildings. The mosque is very photogenic only when you look from the other side of the pond.
Near Town Hall.
Vallikkattu Kavu is a 27-acre sacred grove in a swamp at Edakkara near Elathur.

Kuchesar.x: Kuchesar is a village near Bulandshahr in western Uttar Pradesh.

Kufri.x: Kufri is a tiny hill station in Southern Himachal Pradesh, India.

sights.d: Established in 1992, it is home to native species such as the great Himalayan snow leopard, and varieties of the musk deer.
One can hike through thick forest around Kufri to the Mahasu Peak- the highest peak in Kufri.
The Indira Tourist Park is near the Himalayan Nature Park and provides panoramic view of the locations around.

Kumaranalloor.x: Kumaranalloor is a city in Kerala in India.

sights.d: The place of Goddess Madurai Meenakshi at Kumaranalloor, Kottayam. Considered one of the most important Devi temples among the 108 durgalayas (devi temples) in Kerala.

Kumbakonam.x: Kumbakonam is a town in the Thanjavur district of Tamil Nadu. The town is popular for the Betal Leaf Combination (Vettrilai Cheeval) and for the thick-strong coffee. Nearby Darasuram is famous for Airavatesvara Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

sights.d: A temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, where he is worshipped as Adi Kumbeswarar.
A temple dedicated to Lord Shiva and a . Built during the Chola era, the temple is named after Lord Indra's elephant Airavata.
Named after the famous temple in Varanasi, this temple worships Lord Shiva as Vishvanatha and his consort Parvati as Vishalakshi.

Kumta.x: Kumta small town on western coastal part of Karnatka, India. The best time to visit is in the month of October to January. Kumta is known for its betelnut, cashew, coconut, banana cultivation and fisheries.

sights.d: 15th century fort.

Kundapur.x: Kundapur is a popular town in Udupi district of Karavali refion of Karnataka, India, known for its unique dialect of Kannada and great food.

sights.d: A very lovely beach with white sands and absolute privacy.
A rather unusual beach with the Arabian Sea and the Suparnika River flowing in parallel.
It is a popular local traditional theatrical art.

Kunnamkulam.x: Kunnamkulam is a city in India. It is 24 km from Thrissur, on Kozhikode highway. It can also reached from Guruvayoor, which is 8 km away.

Kurnool.x: Kurnool is a city in Rayalaseema, Andhra Pradesh state. It is home to the 16th-century Konda Reddy Fort.
Kurnool.icon: 23 - Telugu Talli Statue with Kondareddy Buruju as background.JPG

sights.d: Remains of old Kurnool Fort.
Small park with igneous rock formations and a cave museum. This site was used in the making of several Indian movies.
Located in the outskirts of Kurnool (5 km).
Ghat on the banks of Hundri River in Kurnool Town, named after the former Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh state.
The premises of the temple are very pleasant.
There are many temples along the banks of the Tungabhadra River. This river is heavily polluted. It flows through three states: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka.

Kurukshetra.x: Kurukshetra is a holy city in Haryana.

sights.d: The centre has around 10 male and 10 female mugger crocodiles which you can see up close. The guides are very knowledgeable.
sights.img: Marsh Crocodiles basking in the sun.JPG

sights.d: The memoirs of Al Beruni, called 'Kitab-ul-Hind' mentions this sacred water tank. The water tank is dedicated to Lord Shiva.
The Sikh Gurus visited Kurukshetra from time to time. Pilgrims go to the Pundits of their area and sign in their register after taking a bath.
A pilgrimage site, where the Bhagavad Gita was spoken.

Krishnanagar.x: Krishnanagar, formerly Krishnagar, is a city in the Nadia district of West Bengal. At the bank of the Jalangi River, Krishnanagar is an important centre for culture and literature.

sights.d: The Bangalore-based Deccan Herald has written, "“We have clay dolls, toys and even clay sculptures in different parts of India.
It stands out for its distinctive architecture. There are 27 oil paintings describing the life of Jesus Christ. There also is a Protestant church in the same compound.
The Rajbari has a beautiful Durga temple in the courtyard. Jhulan Mela is celebrated in July-August, Baro Dol is held 12 days after Dol Purnima in March-April.

Koyilandy.x: Koyilandy or Quilandy/Quilandi is a town in Kozhikode District, in the Malabar region of Kerala, India. The population is 72,000 (2011).

sights.d: Vasco de Gama arrived in India at this place. There is a memorial and a park in this beautiful beach.
This 480-metre bridge is the longest bridge in Kozhikode district. Completed in 2015, it has 13 spans. The surroundings are lush, green and very photogenic.
With beautiful pond.
Non-profit organization intervening in health, education, relief work and rural development. Established in 1915 by Swamy Nirmalananda of Kolkata.
Beautiful views of the river and valleys down. Fogs are common.

Lakhimpur.x: Lakhimpur is a district of Upper Assam and one of the greenest districts in India. It is home to many historical temples and is full of local culture-- seeing a mixture of Aryan and non-Aryan culture. Namghars, temples fill this place.

sights.d: Basudev Than is located in the Dhakuakhana sub-division. Established in the 17th century, this place is worth visiting for history lovers, religion lovers and anyone…
Padumani Than is a visit worthy temple in Lakhimpur, which has a story to tell.
This is a home for many migratory birds, thus making it worth visiting by nature enthusiasts and also for those who simply want to enjoy nature, or have a picnic nearby.
see lord Ganesha on a ship! Shiva Mandir and Durga Mandir are also worth visiting.

Lakkundi.x: Lakkundi is a small village in Karnataka state in India. It is a historical place This small village has many temples with magnificent architecture of Kalyani Chalukya, Hoysala period.
Lakkundi.icon: Jain temple at Lakkundi built in the Kalyani Chalukya style.jpg

Krishnarajanagara.x: Krishnarajanagara or K.R. Nagar is a riverside paddyfield township in Mysore District in Karnataka, India. It was home to 36,000 people in 2011.

sights.d: The old railway station of the British period is not forgotten because that area is still known by the same name.
Beautiful paddyfields and cute little railway station where only slow trains stop six times a day.

Lohgad.x: Lohgad, literally meaning the iron fort, is a hill fort located in the Pune District in South Maharashtra near the hill-station of Lonavala. Because of its strategic location the Lohagad Fort is often considered as the strongest and most famous Deccan forts.

Hanuman Darwaza is the third gateway of the Lohagad Fort. This is probably an older gateway and is said to have been constructed by Aurangzeb in the late 17th century.

Palanpur.x: Palanpur is in North Gujarat, India.

sights.d: 18th-century stepwell which is four-storey deep. Now neglected but still an attraction, it was probably built from material from previous monuments.
According to local legend, the Chaulukya king Siddhraj Jaisimha was born in Palanpur so his mother Mayanalla Devi had ordered to build a stepwell.
A private sports club now. Nawab Sher Mohammed Khan built it to commemorate coronation of British King George V in 1913.
Beautiful large garden built by Nawab Taley Muhammed Khan dedicated to his Australian wife Begum Jahanara aka Joan Falkiner.
Explore the traditional haveli mansions with carved wooden facades and brackets in gated communities called pols in Moti Bazar, Nani Bazar, Jhaveriwad, Teen Batti,…
The four-storied memorial pillar was built in 1936 for Nawab Sher Muhammed Khan by Nawab Taley Mohammed Khan.
In 1750, Nawab Bahadur Khan built a brick and mortar city-walls of Palanpur.
Early Jhalori ruler Malik Mujahid Khan built this lake dedicated to his queen Manbai Jadeja in 1628.

Palnadu.x: Palnadu is a cultural region in southern Andhra Pradesh.

sights.d: The water here is used for crocodile breeding.
A small village near Madhira and Wyra. It has approximately 1000 houses, which includes the 700 houses of Kammas (Chowdaries) and 150 houses of members of Scheduled…
One of the Buddhist sites in Andhra Pradesh, on an island created by the Nagarjuna Sagar Dam.
sights.img: Panaromic view of the buddha statue and other monuments.jpg

sights.d: A Shiva temple atop a sacred hill. Its original name is Kondakavuru, but is more popularly known as Kotappakonda or Trikutaparvatham, a three-peaked hill nearby.
A place of deep mystery attracting many tourists to explore.
One of the sites on the Godavari-Krishna delta region where some of the most famous diamonds were found, collectively called the "Golconda diamonds" after the diamond…

Pakur.x: Pakur is a mining town in the Santhal Parganas region of Jharkhand, close to Birbhum and Murshidabad districts of West Bengal.

sights.d: A memorial park dedicated to the twin leaders of the Santal Rebellion: Sido and Kanhu.

Old Malda.x: Old Malda is a small heritage town near Malda in North Bengal, at the confluence of the Mahananda and Kalindi rivers. Most of the town is developed along parallel streets lined up by old homes.

sights.d: Although the original mosque was built during the rule of Bengal sultan Hussain Shah, the present building was built during the rule of Mughal emperor Akbar in 1004 AH.
The gurudwara was established in 1996 to mark the legendary visit of Guru Nanak who halted at Malda on his way to Puri.
A 400-year-old temple with a stone altar. The Shyam Rai deity is placed on the altar every year during Holi (Doljatra) and Krishna Janmashtami.

Panipat.x: Panipat is a city in the state of Haryana in the Plains region of India. An industrial city in modern times, its main claim to fame is that the First Battle of Panipat in 1526 was a key step in establishing the Mughal Empire.

sights.d: A mosque and garden built by first Mughal emperor Babur to commemorate his victory over Ibrahim Lodi.
The last ruler of the Lodi dynasty, Ibrahim Lodi's tomb is quite a simple looking rectangular tomb with a small flight of steps.
A memorial to 16th century King Hemu, who defeated the Mughals in October 1556 and briefly took control of Delhi before being defeated in a repeat battle around a month…
The site of the Third Battle of Panipat between the Marathas and Afghans. According to legend, it was marked by a black mango tree which has since disappeared.

Papanasam.x: Papanasam is near to Tirunelveli and Tenkasi at about 40 km, in Tamil Nadu, India. It is famous for a Sivan kovil (a type of temple) and the river Tamirabarani flows here.

Paradip.x: Paradip or Paradeep is a major port town in the North Coast of Odisha.

sights.d: You can visit in the Evening Only

Paravur.x: Not to be confused with North Paravur, which is approximately 175 km to the north. Paravur is in Quilon/Kollam district, Kerala, Southern Travancore, India. It is a municipal town connected to Thiruvananthapuram and Quilon by trains and bus.The population is around 44,000 (2011).
Paravur.banner: Local fisherman at Paravur beach - panoramio (cropped).jpg

sights.d: A famous religious place. This church's festival takes place at the last week of October every year. Sunday mass is 7:30AM.

Parumala.x: Parumala is a small town in Pathanamthitta district in Kerala in India. This is an island in Pampa River. Mannar is a small town across the Pampa river near Parumala.

sights.d: It is here that Geevarghese Mar Gregorios, the first declared saint of The Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church, is entombed.
Temple considered one of the oldest in Kerala.

Paschim Medinipur.x: Paschim Medinipur or West Midnapore is a district of West Bengal. It was once a part of Midnapore district until 2003, which got split into two districts: Paschim Medinipur and Purba Medinipur.

Pathankot.x: Pathankot is a city and district in the Indian state of Punjab.

sights.d: Fortress built by the Pathania Rajputs, more than 900 years ago. It was damaged due to the great earthquake which struck this region early in 1905 AD.
The fort is one of the main attractions of Pathankot city. It was built in 1505 AD by a Rajput chief, by the name of Jaspal Singh Pathania.
An important ancient Shiva temple 30 km from Pathankot towards Indora/Chanour (HP).

Patiala.x: Patiala is a city in Punjab, India. Patiala is a lively city known for its production of handcrafted goods. The juttis, traditional embroidered shoes for women and men alike, are exported all over the world to the Punjabi diaspora.

sights.d: The gardens were designed in 1876 by Kaur Sahib Ranbir Singh, the younger brother of the Maharaja.
The Palace, built in the mid-19th century, was the seat of the Patiala royal family. With over 1,000 rooms it's one of the largest royal residences in the world.
Qila Mubarak was the official residence of the Maharaja till 1862. The complex comprises 10 courtyards and several historic built structures.
A 620-ha reserve protecting home to wild boars, partridges, hares, owlets, jungle cats, and hog deer.

Parassinikkadavu.x: Parassinikkadavu is a small riverside tourist town in Kannur District, Kerala, India. This is the only temple where the mild alcoholic drink called 'Toddy' is offered to the God at the temple.

sights.d: You can get an auto (₹20) for a ride down the winding road to the temple. Alternatively there is a direct footpath with wide steps.
Theyyam is performed in the temples of Parassinikkaavu and surrounding cities during certain times of the year.
You can go across the Vellikkeel Bridge by hiring an auto-rickshaw from Bakkalam to Pattuvam (₹200). Very beautiful mangrove swamps and an estuary.
Scenic mosque in the middle of a paddy field.
Traditional blacksmith workshop is the main attraction. There is a lighthouse in this island.

Pattambi.x: Pattambi is a small town inhabited by 28,000 people in Palakkad District of Malabar region, in Kerala state, India. The town is famous for its rich lineage in literature.

sights.d: A unique and terrific festival, which is celebrated by all residents of Pattambi harmoniously.

Panitanki.x: Panitanki is a village in the Darjeeling district of West Bengal, India.

Panihati.x: Panihati, or colloquially Peneti, is a heritage town in the North 24 Parganas district of West Bengal, on the Hooghly River.
Panihati.icon: Barrackpore Trunk Road - Panihati - North 24 Parganas 2012-04-11 9471.JPG

sights.d: A row of 12 Shiva temples along the Hooghly River.
A "pancharatna" (five-pinnacled) temple dedicated to Radha-Krishna. The temple premise resembles that of Dakshineswar with a row of Shiva temples at riverside and a ghat…
sights.img: Premises of Thakurbari of Giribala dasi at Agarpara in Panihati Municipality of North 24 Parganas district 20.jpg
Saheb Bagan Bari premises near Saheb Bagan Ghat at Panihati in North 24 Pargana district, West Bengal 03.jpg

sights.d: Founded in 1921 by Satish Chandra Dasgupta, a close aide of Mahatma Gandhi.
One of the elegant edifices on the Hooghly River. It originally belonged to Asutosh De or Chatu Babu, one of the figures of the 19th-century Bengali Renaissance.

Pandua (Malda).x: Pandua, also known as Adina, is a medieval citadel in the Northern Plains‎ of West Bengal, India. It is known for its massive Adina Masjid along with the ruins of a couple of mosques, tombs and darghas. A trip to Pandua can be combined with a trip to the nearby citadel of Gour with Malda as the base.
Pandua (Malda).icon: Adina Mosque at Malda district of West Bengal 04.jpg

sights.d: Built in 1369 by Sultan Sikander Shah and during that time it was the largest mosque in India. The courtyard measures by . The entrance is through an insignificant door.
sights.img: Adina Mosque at Malda district of West Bengal 08.jpg

sights.d: Eklakhi Tomb or Mausoleum houses constructed by Sultan Jalaluddin Mohammad Shah in around 1425 at a cost of rupees one lakh (hundred thousand) and hence the name.
sights.img: Eklakhi Mausoleum at Pandua in Malda district 02.jpg

sights.d: Locally known as Chota Sona Masjid, the Qutb Sahi Mosque is built in honour of Saint Nur Qutb-ul-Alam.
sights.img: Qutub Shahi Mosque at Pandua in Malda district 01.jpg

sights.d: A well-preserved wildlife sanctuary with spotted deer and nilgais. This is controlled by the West Bengal Forest Department and one can witness migratory birds during…
sights.img: Deers at Adina Deer Park, Malda.jpg

sights.d: This hammam was once part of the royal complex of the Illiyas Shah dynasty. Nothing much remains of the royal hammam.
This too is located near the deer park. This minar standing on a small mound was part of the defensive system of the royal enclosure of Pandua during the Illiyas Shah…

Paschim Bardhaman.x: Paschim Bardhaman, literally "West Bardhaman", is the western coal-rich industrial district of West Bengal. Fondly known as the "Ruhr of India", Paschim Bardhaman is home to two steel cities, a coal mining centre, and a locomotive workshop.

Panskura.x: Panskura, a town along the Kangsabati River in West Bengal, is famous for the state's "Valley of Flowers". It's a popular weekend getaway for Kolkata residents in spring.

sights.d: A secluded village, often called the "Valley of Flowers" of West Bengal.

Pandhurna.x: Pandhurna is a small town on the banks of the Jam River in Madhya Pradesh, India. It's not a place that shows up on the usual India tourist trail, and honestly, most of the year there's not a whole lot happening here. But once a year, for one single evening, this quiet orange-farming town turns into the site of one of the strangest and most talked-about festivals in the country.

sights.d: Celebrated every year on Bhadrapada Amavasya (new moon) on the second day of Pola festival.

Pandya Nadu.x: Pandya Nadu consists of the homeland of the Pandya dyansty as well as the southernmost point of mainland India.

Prayagraj.x: Prayagraj, formerly Allahabad, is one of the holiest cities in India, is in Uttar Pradesh. The city is famous for being the site of the confluence of the holy rivers Ganges and Yamuna; and also the Hindu pilgrimage Kumbh Mela, the largest gathering of humans on the planet holding hundreds of millions of pilgrims every 12 years.

sights.d: The Allahabad Fort, built from the year 1583 onwards by Akbar, stands at the junction of the two great rivers.
It is the seat of Justice in Uttar Pradesh, and is the oldest high court in the country with largest strength of judges.
The marvelous monuments is perched in Company Garden. The monument served as the house of the legislative assembly during the British era, when Allahabad was the capital…
sights.img: Thornhill Mayne Memorial, Alfred Park, Allahabad.jpg

sights.d: Khusro Bagh is a walled Mughal styled garden and burial chamber located just south of the Allahabad (Prayagraj) Junction station.
The 4th oldest university of India, it has various neo-Gothic monuments. The university originally started as the Muir College in 1872.
The New Yamuna Bridge Naini is located west of the Old Naini Bridge and is parallel to it. The cable styled bridge came up in 2004 had provides 6 lane road traffic.
Spot for the lovers of ancient history. Prayagraj being a historical city, the museum offers a convenient way to explore the history of the city and vicinity.
Learn about the intricacies of Indian struggle for freedom during the early 20th century.

Pawapuri.x: Pawapuri, 101 kilometers from Patna and 38 kilometers from Rajgir, or Pava is a holy site for Jains.

sights.d: A marble temple, the Jalmandir, was later built in the middle of the tank, and is now a major pilgrimage spot for Jains.

Pettavaithalai.x: Pettavaithalai is in the Central Tamil Nadu region of India. It is located between Kulithalai and Tiruchirappalli. The town is an important pilgrimage location.

Pilibhit.x: Pilibhit is a city in Uttar Pradesh in India. It is 48 km from Bareilly and is the greenest area.

sights.d: The protected forest holds an amazing ecosystem of over 400 square miles and provides a good prey base for the elegant cats.
sights.img: Sultan- largest amongst all the tigers at PTR.png

Plains (India).x: The Plains of India are the country's heartland. Also called the Hindi Belt, this region contains the large and politically significant states of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, and the country's capital, New Delhi. With an area of about 400,000 square kilometres (150,000 sq mi), the Plains are the home of about half a billion people (about one in every sixteen people alive today), including the densely-populated cities of Delhi, Lucknow, Varanasi and Patna.
Plains (India).icon: Scindia Ghat in morning, Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh, India (2012).jpg

Pollachi.x: Pollachi is a town and a municipality close to the foothills of Western Ghats in Tamil Nadu, 40 km south of Coimbatore. It is picture perfect for the nomenclature — Mini Kodambakkam. Though prominently known for cash crops, coconuts and second biggest ‘sandhai’ (market) in the country, the town has now become famous for cinema shootings and consequently a huge tourist attraction.

sights.d: It is the home of the Vethathiri Maharishi Kundalini Yoga and Kayakalpa Research Foundation, founded by Shri Vethathiri Maharishi in 1985.
Aliyar (ஆழியார் azhiyar) Dam is a reservoir 27 km away from pollachi on the foothills of Valparai, in the Anamalai range of the Western Ghats.
This place is 20 km from Thirumoorthy dam. One must take the left road near Chinnar check-post (Tamilnadu side) along Udumalpet - Munnar road, to reach this place.
Masani Amman Temple is situated at a distance of 15 km from Pollachi. This sanctified shrine attracts large number of devotees.
Monkey Falls is located at the 29th KM junction on the Pollachi-Valparai road.
Lying adjacent to the Indira Gandhi Wild Life Sanctuary, the 285 sq km stretch of forest known as Parambikulam Tiger Reserve (formerly Parambikulam Wildlife Sanctuary)…

Pondicherry.x: Pondicherry, also known as Puducherry or Pondy, is a city in Southern India. There is a strong French influence on the architecture of the city, especially in the old quarters, with rues and boulevards lined with Mediterranean-style houses and bakeries, although the city remains very much Indian. French is still understood, and the whole city makes for a pleasant mix of the East and the West.

sights.d: There's a white monument at the centre of the park called Aayi Mandapam. It was built during the time of Napoleon III.
The largest lake of Pondicherry and home to around 200 species of birds.
A nice park, though a little in disarray. An aquarium, maintained by the Directorate of Fisheries, is also a must-see while in the garden.
A lighthouse was constructed in Pondicherry in the nineteenth century by the French rulers.
A war memorial dedicated to the French Indians who died for the country during the First World War.
An art and history museum with its collection of fine lost wax bronzes from the Chola period.
One of the most common reason to visit Pondicherry is to visit this ashram of the spiritual leader Sri Aurobindo.
sights.img: Sri Aurobindo Ashram, a spiritual ashram of Sri Aurobindo in Pondicherry 05.jpg

sights.n: Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Jesus
sights.d: An oriental specimen of Gothic Revival architecture. It contains rare stained glass panels depicting events from the life of Christ and saints of the Catholic Church.

Pondicherry (union territory).x: Pondicherry, officially Puducherry, is a union territory in Southern India. It consists of four enclaves in three different states, which came under French occupation before they were peacefully handed over to India. Each enclave shares a mixed cultural heritage, combining its South Indian roots with a French colonial past.

Porbandar.x: Porbandar is a city in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat, India. It is the historical birthplace of Mahatma Gandhi, and the mythical birthplace of Sudama, the childhood friend of the Hindu god Krishna. The majority of the people here belong to Kharwa community which mainly deals with fishing as their profession.

Pragpur.x: Pragpur is a small heritage village situated in Kangra district of Himachal Pradesh.

Pudukkottai.x: Pudukkottai is in Tamil Nadu. Pudukkottai is also known as Archaeologist's Paradise. It is one of the oldest human settlements in south India.

sights.d: The most ornate temple in Pudukkottai district, full of bursting baroque sculptures. It is the temple of Athmanatha.
sights.img: Gopuram of Avudayar Koil behind tree.jpg

sights.d: A fort constructed by Vijaya Raghunatha Sethupathi, the Raja of Ramnad in 1687.
The museum was opened in 1910 by the Thondaiman Rulers. It is one of the largest museums in Tamil Nadu.
The temple complex includes a 1000-pillared hall and has many inscriptions by the Pallava king Mahendravarman including a treatise on music.
Living places of Jains. The place is almost 800 years old. Nearby lake and boating. Nicely landscaped garden.

Puliangudi.x: Puliangudi is a city in Tenkasi District on the NH 208 highway connecting Thirumangalam (near Madurai) with Kollam in Kerala. Located on the foothills of the Western ghats, is one of the fast emerging options as a base for the Sankaran Kovil-Courtallam tourist circuit midway between the two. It is also known for lemon cultivation.

Punalur.x: Punalur is a town and a municipality in Kerala in India.

sights.d: An important pilgrim center. Famous for its Sastha temple with a Sastha installed several centuries before the Christian Era.
Known for its cattle market.
Famous as Muslim pilgrim center.
Huge rock. Legend says Jatayu, the giant bird in the epic Ramayana, fell after failing in its attempt to stop Ravana from taking sita away. Ideal place for trekking.
One of the famous waterfall in Kerala.
Famous for its ancient Bhagavathy temple.

Pune.x: Pune, formerly Poona, is the second-largest city in the Indian state of Maharashtra. Often considered as the cultural capital of Maharashtra, Pune is known for its educational tourism and has a blend of cultural, business, health, and cuisine tourism background. The city also houses fantastic restaurants, good museums, and hill forts which offer panoramic views.

Pulwama.x: Pulwama is a town in Pulwama district in the Kashmir Valley, in central Jammu and Kashmir in India.

Payyanur.x: Payyanur is a town on the Perumba river in Kannur District, in the Malabar region of Kerala, India.

sights.d: Curvaceous palm fringed beach with rocky surroundings. Near Kannurgate of Naval Academy.
Majestic white building in a sprawling campus
very scenic place.
Rich people live here.
Big and beautiful temple.
very green and scenic

Poovankurichi.x: Poovankurichi or Poovan Kurichi is a hamlet in the district of Tirunelveli near Ambasamudram, Tamil Nadu, India. The village is located 50 km west of Tirunelveli town and 30 km from Tenkasi.

Pileru.x: Pileru (also known as Piler) is a town in Annamayya district of the Rayalaseema region of Andhra Pradesh, India. It is located on the banks of the Pileru River and serves as a connecting point between Tirupati and Rayalaseema. The town is surrounded by small hills and greenery and is known for its peaceful rural vibe.

Poovar.x: Poovar is a small coastal village at the southernmost tip of Thiruvananthapuram district in Southern Travancore in Kerala, South India. Its name is derived from the Malayalam words poo (flower) and ar (river) which translates as "River of Flowers," a name bestowed by Marthanda Varma, the 18th-century king of Travancore, in recognition of the fragrant flowers that once floated down the Neyyar River to reach the sea here. What makes Poovar genuinely singular is a rare geographical convergence: the Neyyar River, a freshwater lake, the backwater canals, and the Arabian Sea all meet within a few hundred metres of each other.

Punjab (India).x: This article covers the Indian state of Punjab. For the Pakistani province, see Punjab (Pakistan). For a general background on the pre-partition region, see Punjab.

Punjabi phrasebook.x: Punjabi/Panjabi is the language of the Punjab/Panjab regions of Pakistan and India. In India, it is written predominantly in the native Gurmukhi alphabet. In Pakistan, it is written in a slightly modified version of the Urdu alphabet called Shahmukhi.

Purba Medinipur.x: Purba Medinipur or East Midnapore is a coastal district of West Bengal. It was once a part of Midnapore district until 2003, which got split into two districts: Paschim Medinipur and Purba Medinipur.

Puri.x: Puri, also known as Jagannath Puri (the Abode of Lord Jagannath) or Purushottama Puri, is a seaside pilgrimage town in the Indian state of Odisha. It is a major tourist destination with the famous temple of Lord Jagannath (means Lord of the World) and a very long beach offering beautiful and pleasant sights. There are many hotels; most overseas tourists stay near the beach.

sights.d: The 8-km long beach of Puri is ideal for surfing and cool for a dip. The beach is covered in golden sand. The waves can also be high and rough during the full moon.
One of the Char Dham temples, i.e. most sacred pilgrimage places of Hindus.
The destination of the Ratha Yatra from Jagannath Temple. It is occupied by Lord Jagannath and his siblings for seven days every year.
Dedicated to Lord Shiva, is said to be the place where Lord Shiva hid himself from Shani, under a pond.
This road is in superb condition. It is peppered with deserted beaches and many rivers flow into the sea in places visible, if not accessible, from the road.
Literally, "the gateway to heaven", Swargadwar is the site of the cremation of almost all famous Odia people. There are good hotels and restaurants near the crematorium.

Purulia.x: Purulia is the headquarters of the Purulia district of West Bengal.

sights.d: An abandoned airfield used by the United States Army Air Forces during the Burma Campaign (1944-1945) of World War II.
Good place for relaxation.
A research centre and library. It was inaugurated in 1960 by central minister Humayun Kabir in 1960.

Pushkar.x: Pushkar is a holy city in Rajasthan, India famous for its Brahma temple, lake, ghats, and bazaar.
Pushkar.icon: Pushkar, India, Panoramic view of Pushkar.jpg

sights.d: Pushkar Lake is a beautiful, sanctified spot in the centre of Pushkar. It is said to have been created by Lord Brahma and is therefore a place of pilgrimage for the…
A temple dedicated to Shiva with an underground component.
A beautiful Shiva temple.
One of the very few temples in the world dedicated to Brahma. Read up on Hinduism to learn why this temple is such a rarity! No matter where you stay in Pushkar, you…
A beautiful temple on a hill dedicated to Gayatri, one of the 2 consorts of Brahma.
A Vishnu temple built in South Indian style that is very different from other temples in North India. Poojas are performed here by Iyengars of Tamil Nadu.

Puttaparthi.x: Puttaparthi is the place in Andhra Pradesh, India where the guru Sathya Sai Baba lived until his death in 2011. He is considered as "God Incarnate" by many of his followers. It is a beautiful valley between the hills.

Puttur.x: Puttur is a city in Dakshina Kannada, a coastal region of the Indian province of Karnataka.

sights.d: chocolate factory
This place is one of India's rare hot water springs.

Raipur.x: Raipur is the largest city in Chhattisgarh. It had been the seat of government of the state until the formation of Naya Raipur. There is not a great deal for visitors to see with most tourists visiting the surrounding region.

sights.d: A small but well maintained museum with exhibits on the history of the state and an impressive collection of carvings, upstairs has a display of tribal artifacts and…
A large statue in the center of a somewhat shabby lake (under refurbishment).

Rajahmundry.x: Rajahmundry, officially Rajamahendravaram, a city in central Andhra Pradesh, is the state's cultural capital. The city is the birthplace of Nannayya, a Telugu poet.
Rajahmundry.icon: Rail Cum Road Bridge on Godavari at Rajahmundry.jpg

sights.d: Art gallery of a famous artist Damerla Ramarao now managed by State Government of Andhra Pradesh.

Rajapalayam.x: Rajapalayam is a city in Tamil Nadu. It attracts travelers seeking seeking an authentic South Indian experience, particularly the scenery of the Western Ghats foothills.
Rajapalayam.icon: SE View Rajapalayam South Tamil Nadu Aug24 A7CR 02018.jpg

Rajgir.x: Rajgir (or Rajagriha) is a city in Bihar in India. It is 15 km from the ruins of Nalanda University, and 100 km from Patna, the capital of the state.

sights.d: The place is atop a small hill and believed to be a meditating place of Buddha.
This archeological site is believed to be the jail in which King Ajatshatru imprisoned his father Bimbisara.
The Chariot Route and shell inscriptions consist of two parallel furrows cut deep into the rock ground for about thirty feet and are believed to have been made by Lord…
Believed to be 2500 years old, these Cyclopean walls are a 40 km long and 4 metres wide fortification running around the city.
This is the shrine of a Muslim Sufi Saint Makhdum Shah and has warm springs similar to Tapodharma.
Dating 1st century CE, the Maniar Matth is said to be a monastery of a cult which worshipped snakes.

Raichur.x: Raichur is a city of 232,000 people (2011) in Northern Karnataka.

sights.d: A hill fort surrounded on three sides by a double row of low circuit walls. It was built without the any cementing material.
A town 5 km from Raichur city, known for its historically important fort, Vishnu temple, two life size elephants carved in white granite and other monuments

Raiganj.x: Raiganj is a town in northern West Bengal, famous for the bird sanctuary along the Kulik River with different species of birds.

sights.d: One of the significant historical buildings of Uttar Dinajpur, on the banks of the Nagar River and near the border of Bihar.
sights.img: Bahin Rajbari in Uttar Dinajpur district 02.jpg

sights.d: A Mughal-style mosque built in 1425 and owned by the Mohanta family.
sights.img: Mohanta Maszid at Barua village near Goyalpara under Raiganj sub-division of Uttar Dinajpur district. 06.jpg

sights.d: A dargah of Syed Burhan, built around 1758. Syed Burhan was a leader of the Fakir-Sannyasin rebellion of the late 18th century.
sights.img: Pirpukur Darga at Ukilpara area of Raiganj town in Uttar Dinajpur district 01.jpg

sights.d: The cathedral of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Raiganj and one of the few churches in sub-Himalayan North Bengal.
Several types of migratory birds arrive here each year from South Asia and coastal regions. They start arriving in June.
The museum has a collection of pottery works, terracotta sculptures and Surjapuri (a Bengali/Maithili dialect) manuscripts.

Purba Bardhaman.x: Purba Bardhaman, literally "East Bardhaman", is a fertile district of central West Bengal. It is bordered by Birbhum and Murshidabad on the north, Nadia on the east, Hooghly on the south, Bankura on the southwest, and Paschim Bardhaman on the west.

Raghunathpur.x: Raghunathpur is a town in the Purulia district of West Bengal.
Raghunathpur.icon: Terracotta panel of the Aat Chala temple of Anchkoda, Raghunathpur, Purulia. 08.jpg

sights.d: A hill that became popular for being the location of Satyajit Ray's various films, including Gupi Gayen Bagha Bayen and Hirak Rajar Deshe.

Puthanathani.x: Puthanathani is a census town in the Malappuram metropolitan area. It is also one of the major commercial towns under the Malappuram urban agglomeration of Malappuram District in Kerala, India. The town lies on the National Highway 66, between Kottakkal and Valanchery.

sights.d: waterfall.
Village.
Street
Communal Harmony Village.
Bypass (road).

Rajkot.x: Rajkot is a city in the state of Gujarat in Western India. Rajkot rather appeals to spiritual tastes. As in Ahmedabad, many ashrams, that offers the teachings of yoga and meditative retreat, are located in the city and its surroundings, amidst forested hills and beautiful lakes.

sights.d: The Watson Museum was established in 1888 and was named after the British Political Agent of Kathiwad, Colonel John Watson.
Where Mahatma Gandhi got his primary education. The buildings were built by the Nawab of Junagadh and took the name of the Duke Alfred of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha

Rajpura.x: Rajpura is a city in the Malwa region of Punjab state in India.

Rameswaram.x: Rameswaram is a town on Pamban Island, in Southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu. It's known for Ramanathaswamy Temple, a Hindu pilgrimage site with ornate corridors, huge sculpted pillars and sacred water tanks. Together with Varanasi, it is considered to be one of the holiest places in India for Hindus and part of the Char Dham (four abodes) pilgrimage.

sights.d: Renowned for its magnificent prakaras or corridors with massive sculptured pillars on either side.

Ranaghat.x: Ranaghat is a small town along the river Churni in the Nadia district of West Bengal. The name Ranaghat comes from the name of a Dakat Rana. This is the great character of Vande Mataram by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.
Ranaghat.banner: Exquisite beauty of Rural Bengal, Churni River (cropped).jpg

Ranchi.x: Ranchi is the capital of the Indian state of Jharkhand.

sights.d: It gives an excellent 360-degree view of the city. A must visit.

An aquarium, game parlour and food court are worth seeing and good values.

sights.n: Yogoda Satsanga Society of India- Ashram
sights.d: Paramahansa Yogananda, the author of Autobiography of a Yogi, began his life's work here. The natural beauty and peaceful atmosphere offer refreshment to mind and spirit.
An arts and cultural heritage museum showcasing Jharkhand's rich history.

Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary.x: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary is near Srirangapatna, Mandya District, Karnataka, India.
Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary.icon: Islands River Ranganathittu Srirangapatna Jan24 A7C 09120.jpg

Rangia.x: Rangia or Rangiya is a city of 96,000 people (2017) in Assam, not far from the Bhutanese border. Rangia is also known my multiple names , including as the City of Colors, Plantation Valley of Assam, Transportation Hub of Assam, Gateway to the Indo-Bhutan Border. The Baralia River flows through the heart of the city, Rangia is also the sub-district and divisional headquarters of North-East Frontier Railway.

Raxaul.x: Raxaul or Raxual is a border town in the Bhojpur region of the state of Bihar, India.
Raxaul.banner: Raxaul Panorama View from Bypass Flyover NH28A (cropped).jpg

Tarapith.x: Tarapith is a temple town in the central region of West Bengal, India. It is a major Hindu pilgrimage centre and several thousand devotees visit the temple every day.

sights.d: Named after Sadhak Banakshyapa.
It is an auspicious place well known for its tantric rituals.
You can see a graceful environment at Bamdev Sangha Ashram.

Ramanattukara.x: Ramanattukara is a town in Kozhikode District, in Kerala. Ramanattukara is a busy junction where the roads coming Palakkad and Trivandrum meet and join together towards Kozhikode.

Beautiful little temple in a very photogenic riverside location.

Ratanpura.x: Ratanpura is a village in Rajgarh tehsil of Churu district in Rajasthan. This village was established in 1848. It is situated 45 km northeast of Churu city and 17 km southwest of Rajgarh.

Ratnagiri.x: Ratnagiri is in the South Konkan region of Maharashtra, Western India.

An area where river meets to sea. The village near this place is Bhatye, so known as Bhatyachi Khadi. The place is beautiful with a view of river & sea both.
A clean seashore and Ganpati temple, about 30 km North from Ratnagiri. This temple is reconstructed in Rajasthani stones and look.

The temple built by Swatantryaveer Savarkar for patit class of people.
