Ratlam.x: Ratlam is a city in the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh.

sights.d: A major Jain temple centred around the first tirthankara (spiritual teacher) of Jainism, Adinath.
The garden is not very big but well maintained and is quite different from most other gardens you are likely to come across.

Raniganj.x: Raniganj is a town in the Paschim Bardhaman district of West Bengal.

Rajnagar (Bihar).x: Rajnagar is a historic town in the Mithila region of northern Bihar, India, near the town of Madhubani. Once a prominent seat of royalty and architectural innovation, it is now known primarily for the sprawling ruins of the Rajnagar Palace Complex, built during the early 20th century by Maharaja Rameshwar Singh of the Darbhanga Raj family. Though now in a dilapidated state, the palace ruins remain a symbol of the grandeur and cultural sophistication of the Mithila region.

sights.d: The primary reason to visit Rajnagar is to witness the hauntingly beautiful ruins of the once-grand palace.

Rejinagar.x: Rejinagar is a town in Murshidabad, West Bengal.

sights.d: Mir Madan was one of the generals of Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah who died in the Battle of Plassey in 1757.

Rayagada.x: Rayagada is a town in South Odisha, close to Andhra Pradesh. It is one of Odisha's many hilly spots.

sights.d: A suspension bridge over the Nagavali River, with scenic views of the river and the surrounding hills.
A beautiful temple with Ratha Yatra organised every year.

Rasikbil.x: Rasikbil, a lake in North Bengal, is popular among birdwatchers for migratory birds. There's an aquarium, deer park and a gharial rehabilitation centre as well.
Rasikbil.icon: Rasikbil bird Sanctuary in Cooch Behar District 3.jpg

Ramanathapuram.x: Ramanathapuram or Ramnad, a town in southern Tamil Nadu, is the gateway to Rameswaram and Dhanushkodi.

sights.d: The palace of the Sethupathi family.

Rewa.x: Rewa is a city in northeastern Madhya Pradesh, India, with a rich history and cultural significance. The city is home to the White Tiger Safari, a major tourist attraction. Additionally, The city hosts several historical sites, including the Rewa Fort and Govindgarh Palace, which reflect its architectural and cultural heritage.
Rewa.icon: Rewa Gate or Jhula Darwaza in the 1880s.jpg

Rewari.x: Rewari is a city in Haryana, 80 km south of New Delhi.

sights.d: This museum holds the oldest surviving steam locomotives, including the Fairy Queen.

Rishikesh.x: Rishikesh, a small town in the northern Indian state of Uttarakhand, is famously known as the "yoga capital" (or "Yog Nagari"). Scenically located where the Ganges comes down from the Himalayas, Rishikesh catapulted to Western fame when the Beatles dropped by for a visit to Maharishi Mahesh Yogi's ashram.

sights.d: One of the temples set up by 'Adiguru Shankaracharya' during the 12th century.
Place of Guru Shri Ram Sukh Daasji (the great thinker of his time) and popular among the Hindu Brahmin community.
One of the most sacred temples in Rishikesh. Located on hill over Swarg Ashram at a height of 1,675 m.
One of the few ashrams left in India where children get the Vedas education. A must-visit in the evening for the Pooja/Aarti, at 5PM in winter and 6PM in summer.
Swargashram (Heavenly Abode), as the name connotes, is a beautiful place situated in picturesque surroundings at the foot of Himalayas on the left bank of the Ganges…
It is 13 stories high, with different deities throughout.

Robertsganj.x: Robertsganj is a city in Uttar Pradesh in India. The town was named after the British soldier Frederick Roberts, 1st Earl Roberts. As with much of the Indian plains, the best time to visit is during the cooler months from October to March.

sights.d: A lookout and a picnic area. Great views of the Son Valley.

Roha.x: Roha is a small city in the Raigad district of Maharashtra.

sights.d: The fort is believed to have been built during the Shilahar dynasty and was reconstructed by the great Maratha king Shivaji.

Rohtak.x: Rohtak is a city in Haryana. It is the political capital of Haryana, and ainly famous for reputed educational institutes, cloth market and dairies.

sights.d: The Tilyar lake is spread over 132 acres. To attract people, there's a restaurant and a mini zoo with bears, tigers, panthers, deer, birds monkeys etc, a toy train for…

Roorkee.x: Roorkee is a small town in the northern Indian state of Uttarakhand. It is approximately 170 km from the capital of India, New Delhi.

sights.d: It is one of the largest yoga institutes in India, possibly the whole world. Named after the Rishi Patanjali, the institute is Baba Ramdev's flagship project.

Rourkela.x: Rourkela is the main centre of trade in the Sundergarh district and state of Odisha (formerly known as Orissa).

sights.d: This is the highest waterfall of Odisha and among the highest of India. Khandadhar means the edge of a sword. The fall looks like a hanging sword from a distance.

Sagar.x: Sagar is a university city in Madhya Pradesh. There are also many temples, lakes and waterfalls in the vicinity, which has helped establish the city as an important site on the Indian tourist circuit.

Sainthia.x: Sainthia is an economically important city in West Bengal. According to the 2011 Indian census, it is the 4th most populous city in Birbhum district; the city had a population of 44,601.

Salem (India).x: Salem is a city in Tamil Nadu. Nicknamed the Steel City, it is best known in modern times for its steel plant and manufacturing industry. It is also a short trip away from the hills of the Eastern Ghats, offering natural scenic beauty.

Sambalpur.x: Sambalpur is the biggest city in western Odisha (formerly known as Orissa). It is a historically important place, mainly because of the number of freedom fights against the British, Veer Surendra Sai being one of the many who died fighting the British.

sights.d: Longest earth dam in the world. The reservoir forms an artificial lake with an area of 746 km² having a shoreline of over 640 km.

Sanchi.x: Sanchi is a village in central Madhya Pradesh in India, about 9 km southwest of Vidisha and 46 km from Bhopal. It is the site of a great Buddhist stupas listed on UNESCO World Heritage List.

sights.d: The events of Buddha's life are carved in stone on the four gates at east, west, north and south sides of the Stupa.

Rupnagar.x: Rupnagar, formerly called Ropar or Rupar, is a city in the northern part of the Malwa region of the Punjab state of India. It is on the south bank of the Sutlej River and has a population of 50,000.

Saharsa.x: Saharsa is a city in the state of Bihar, beside the city of Darbhanga. Saharsa has many colleges.

Sarnath.x: Sarnath is a holy town in Uttar Pradesh, India, about 13 km north-east of Varanasi. It's famous as the site of the deer park where Gautama Buddha first taught the Dharma and also where the original Sangha was formed. Consequently, it is one of the 4 main Buddhist pilgrimage destinations, and since 2026 the Chaukandi Stupa and the Archaelogical Remains of Sarnath are listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

sights.d: Constructed by king Ashoka in 249 BCE to commemorate his pilgrimage to the Deer Park.

Sasaram.x: Sasaram is a city in the Bhojpur region of Bihar, India. The town contains three tombs of Sur kings and a couple of related monuments. Sasaram lies on the Grand Trunk Road, which was refurbished by Sher Shah Suri.

sights.d: The Tomb of Sher Shah Suri follows the Indo - Islamic form of architecture. It was constructed by Mir Muhammad Alawal Khan and was constructed between 1540 - 45.
Hasan Shah Suri was Sher Shah's father and his tomb lies just east of his son's tomb.
Islam Shah, also known as Salim Shah, is the son of Sher Shah. He is the second ruler of the Sur Dynasty, and ruled from 1545 - 54.
Mir Muhammad Alawal Khan (Alawal Khan) was the architect of the tombs of both Hasan Shah and Sher Shah.

Maa Tara Chandi Temple is one of the "52 Shakti Peetha". The right eye (Netra) is said to have fallen here. It is dedicated to Maa Durga or Maa Shakti.

Satara.x: Satara is a city in South Maharashtra. It was the last seat of the Maratha Empire and contains several of its historical monuments and forts. It is an old city reflected by cobbled streets and old buildings perched upon the hills of the Western Ghats.

Satna.x: Satna is a small town in Madhya Pradesh in India. It has a population of around 300,000. It is famous for its cement factories.

Wardha.x: Wardha is a city of 126,000 people (2011) in Vidarbha. Founded in 1866, the town is now an important center for the cotton trade. It was an important part of Gandhian Era.

sights.d: Old name of village Sevagram was Shegaon. After leaving Sabarmati ashram, Mahatma Gandhi stayed a few days in Wardha City at Bunglow of Jamanalal Bajaj.

Vishwa Shanti Stupa was a dream of Fujii guruji as called by Gandhiji. It is beside Gitai Mandir. It is a large stupa of white color.

West Bengal.x: West Bengal, a state in Eastern India, presents some of the marvellous landscape features and natural scenic beauty, from the picturesque hills of Darjeeling to the mangrove rainforest of the Sundarbans. Here, you can also find man-made structures with varying tastes, from the terracotta temples of Bishnupur to the colonial structures of Kolkata.

Sankarankoil.x: Sankarankoil, or Sankarankovil, is in Tenkasi district in Tamil Nadu.

sights.d: The main deity is half Shiva and half Vishnu to emphasis the equality of both gods. The temple has many good and interesting sculptures.

Goddess Dakshina Kali is worshipped here, atop a steep flight of stairs. Views over Coronation Bridge and Teesta River.

Serampore.x: Serampore is a town in the Hooghly district of West Bengal, on the western bank of the Hooghly River. One of the rare Danish colonies of India, Serampore is unique for its Danish-British-Bengali heritage.

sights.d: The former seat of government of Serampore, originally a home of Ole Bie, who built the Danish colony.
sights.img: Danish Government House at Serampore in West Bengal.jpg

sights.d: The Protestant church was once the centre for all European social and religious events.

The famous Jagannath temple in Serampore, known for organising the oldest Ratha Yatra in Bengal, after the Puri Ratha Yatra.

Sanjay Gandhi National Park.x: The Sanjay Gandhi National Park, formerly the Borivali National Park, is the lungs of Mumbai. It is famous for its leopards and the caves inside the park.

Widely visited by the Digambar sect of the Jain community. It has three huge idols of Lord Adinath and his two sons, Bahubali and Bharat.
The second-largest lake in Mumbai and supplies part of the city's potable water. It is inhabited by mugger crocodiles (Crocodylus palustris).
A group of picturesque hills, an unspoiled and pollution-free area, carpeted by natural foliage and fauna.

Sargachi.x: Sargachi, a village in the Murshidabad district of West Bengal, is best known for its Ramakrishna Mission campus, with its science museum and zoological park.

Sattal.x: Sattal is a cluster of seven interconnected freshwater lakes in the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand, India. Nestled at an altitude of 1,370 m within dense oak and pine forests, it is a tranquil haven for birdwatchers, nature lovers, and those seeking a quiet alternative to the bustling hill stations of Nainital and Bhimtal.

sights.d: The largest and most accessible lake. A boating jetty, a small café, and a short walking path encircle its shore.
Connected to Purna Tal by narrow channels. These smaller, shadier lakes are surrounded by thick foliage and offer secluded spots for birdwatching. Often less crowded.
A tranquil pair, ideal for quiet contemplation. Nal‑Damayanti Tal is the deepest, with clear water reflecting the surrounding hills.
Sukh Tal (“Happy Lake”) is a shallow, lily‑covered pool. Garud Tal is the smallest, often dried up by summer’s end.
Established in the 1930s by Dr. E. Stanley Jones, this serene estate houses a chapel, a guesthouse, and a library.
A beautiful stone church with stained‑glass windows, set amidst tall pines. The quiet churchyard is a place for meditation.

Saraikela.x: Saraikela or Seraikella in South Jharkhand served as the capital of the Singh Deo dynasty. The town is known for the Saraikela version of the famous Chhau dance, a unique style of masked tribal dance.

Shimla.x: Shimla, previously spelt Simla, is the capital of the state of Himachal Pradesh in India. It is a very popular holiday retreat during the summer months and is well known for its Victorian architecture, which is reflected in certain areas of the Mall and the Ridge. It is also a famous holiday spot for honeymoon.
Shimla.banner: Shimla banner Southern Side of Ridge.jpg

sights.d: Constructed in 1846, this is the second oldest church in North India. The stain-glass windows,representing charity, faith, patience, hope, fortitude and humility, and…

Shimoga.x: Shimoga or Shivamogga is a town in the state of Karnataka. The name originates from Shiva-mukha i.e., face of Lord Shiva.

sights.d: Situated on the banks of the River Tunga in the busy lanes of Shimoga is a 16th-century place built by Shivappa Naik of Keladi.
Known for being one of the earliest railway stations in Karnataka. The second railway line of the Mysore Kingdom was a meter gauge line between Shimoga and Birur.

The new legislature assembly complex, called Niyamasabha (Law House in Malayalam), is a modern structure located in heart of the city.

Thiruvayaru.x: Thiruvayaru is a small town in Tamil Nadu.

Tindivanam.x: Tindivanam is a town at the north coast of Tamil Nadu. Tindivanam is a main hub connecting Chennai to southern part of Tamil Nadu. It also connects Kanchipuram to southern Tamil Nadu and Pondicherry with Bangalore.

Tinsukia.x: Tinsukia is the economic capital of Assam and the main business centre of Upper Assam. It is a gateway to many tourist attractions in Upper Assam. It has a couple of good hotels to stay overnight before you embark on a journey to the nearby areas.

sights.d: "Tilinga" means "bell" in the Assamese language. The temple holds a spot in the Limca Book of World Records for hosting one of the largest collections of bells of all…
Na-pukhuri, literally meaning 9 ponds, is a cluster of nine interconnected ponds dating back to 1792.
Guijan Ghat is a scenic riverside area located on the banks of the Dibru River.

Tiruchendur.x: Tiruchendur is in Tamil Nadu, a state in Southern India, on the shores of the Bay of Bengal. This Town is famous for the Temple of Lord Muguran/ Lord Karthikeya/Lord Subramanya (Son of Lord Shiva) As per legend, demon Soorapadhman had become powerful, after obtaining boons from Lord Shiva. His boon was such only the power of Lord Shiva and Devi Parvathi together good destroy him.
Tiruchendur.icon: A tourist enjoy the sunrise, Tiruchendur, India.jpg

sights.d: It is located 10 km from Tiruchendur. A natural water spring in the desert near Ayyanar Temple attracts local tourists.
Kaalikesam is a beautiful place to visit. It is located at a distance of 100 km from Tiruchendur. It's a very good picnic spot.
The Mutharamman temple is located 20 km from Tiruchendur (Thoothukudi Dist) is known for the popular Dasara festival where folk dance artists from all over the state…
It is located 18 km. from Tiruchendur. It is on the sea-shore at the Bay of Bengal.
Manimuthar Falls is a natural waterfall flowing throughout the year situated above the Manimuthar dam.
The cluster of 9 Sacred Srivaishnava Temples located near Tiruchendur are known as Navathirupathis.

Tiruchirappalli.x: Tiruchirappalli, also known as Trichy or Tiruchi, is a city in Tamil Nadu, Southern India. It has a population of 916,857 as of 2011 census. The climate in the city is extremely hot but humidity is low.

sights.d: Constructed in the Dravidian style of architecture, the temple is glorified in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, the early medieval Tamil canon of the Alvar saints from the…
built by the Nawab of Arcot more than two centuries ago.
The mausoleum of a Muslim saint who came to Tiruchirappalli centuries ago.
2,000 yr old dam built on the Kallanai river, (an offshoot of the Cauvery river) by Karikala Cholan.

Tirunelveli.x: Tirunelveli is a city in the state of Tamil Nadu in southern India. The city is administrative headquarters of Tirunelveli District.

sights.n: Bharat Ratna Dr. M.G.R New Bus Stand
sights.d: The bus stand is located in Veinthankulam. It has regular bus services to nearby cities like Tenkasi, Tiruchendur, Thoothukudi, Kanniyakumari, Nagercoil, Kovilpatti as…
The bus stand serves as terminal to Local buses which run within the city. The bus stand is under re-modelling now.
The bus stand, which is loocated in Palayamkottai, also serves as terminal for local buses.

sights.n: Arulmigu Nellaiyappar Sametha Arultharum Gandhimathi Amman Temple
sights.d: Arulmigu Nellaiappar - Ganthimathi Temple is one of the oldest and biggest Shiva temple in Tamil Nadu. It is situated in the heart of Tirunelveli.
The historic temple, which was built by Nayakas, is located in the banks of river Thamirabarani.

Tirupati.x: Tirupati is the spiritual capital of Andhra Pradesh, India. It is most famous for its Sri Venkateswara Temple dedicated to Vishnu, also known as Balaji in Northern India and Govinda in Southern India. The temple is on top of Tirumala hills, while the town is in the foothills.

sights.d: This fort was built in the 11th century. This site features stucco work and abundance natural light.
This temple is a few blocks north from the Tirupati train station.
This is a holy waterfall with a temple dedicated to Venkateshwar near its base.
Millions of pilgrims from all over India and abroad visit the temple of Venkateswara throughout the year. It is regarded as one of the most ancient temples.
Asia's second largest zoo, with an area of 5,500 acres. It is built on the concept of Hindu mythology and exhibits only animals that are mentioned in ancient epics.
Tiruchanur is the abode of Goddess Padmavathi Devi. It is 5 km from Tirupati.

Tiruppur.x: Tiruppur is a city in Tamil Nadu, south India. It is known as the knitwear capital of India because the city accounts for 90% of India's cotton knitwear exports from the country.

Tirur.x: Tirur is a town in Malappuram District, in the Malabar region of Kerala, in India. The town is 43 km south of Kozhikode. It is a major trading centre of fish and betel, and is known as the birthplace of the poet Thunchath Ezhuthachan.

sights.d: Hindu temple, one of oldest Bhadrakaali temples in Kerala. The Vairankode Vela, celebrated here, is one of the most popular local annual festivals.
Birth place of the great poet Thunchath Ezhuthachan, considered as the Father of the Malayalam literature.
A large river bank on shores of River Nila. This river bank hold stories of the biggest Hindu festival of South India- Mamankam (similar to Kumbh Mela of North), which…

Tiruttani.x: Tiruttani is in Tiruvallur district of northern Tamil Nadu, India. It is most famous for its Sri Subramanya Temple dedicated to Murugan, on top of Tiruttani hills, while the town is on the foothills.

sights.d: Karimalai Aarupdai Murugan Temple is a temple which consists of six Lord Murugan statue in one place. It's called "Aarupadai". This is a must place to see.

Tiruvallur.x: Tiruvallur is a town in the southern state of Tamil Nadu, India. It is nearly 45 km west of Chennai, the capital city of Tamil Nadu. It is en route to Tirupati, the abode of Lord Balaji.

sights.d: This temple is situated in the heart of the city. The lord is considered as a form of Vishnu, one of the principal deities in Hinduism.
Karimalai Aarupdai Murugan Temple is a temple which consists of six Lord Murugan statue in one place. It's called "Aarupadai". This is a must place to see.

Tiruvannamalai.x: Tiruvannamalai, also known as Arunachala, is one of the greatest Saivite shrines in Tamil Nadu, India, on a sprawling 24 acre temple campus, drawing hundreds of thousands of pilgrims every full moon. The hill here is considered to be a manifestation of Shiva. Tiruvannamalai is one of the Panchabhoota Stalams signifying the 5 elements of wind (Kalahasti), water (Tiruvanaikkal), fire (Tiruvannamalai), earth (Thiruvarur) and space (Chidambaram).

sights.d: The major tourist and religious destination of the town. The temple has several tall towers in a symmetric arrangement.
Situated just outside the town.
Situated just outside the town. This is basically a cave where the saint meditated in his early days of enlightenment.
In addition to the Arunachaleswara temple, there are nine small "Shivalayams" (Lord Shiva temples) along the Girivalam path, each representing the "navagrahas".
Pournami (Full Moon) Day and Karthigai Deepam Festival
The most popular activity in Tiruvannamalai is "Girivalam", which is walking barefoot around the Tiruvannamalai hill.

Thiruvarur.x: Thiruvarur, the headquarters of the Thiruvarur district of Tamil Nadu, was an important Chola town, as Manu Needhi Chola ruled from here. It is also the birthplace of Carnatic musicians Tyagaraja, Muthuswamy Dikshitar and Shyama Shastri.

sights.d: The ancient Thyagaraja Temple at Thiruvarur is dedicated to the Somaskanda aspect of Shiva.
It is the oldest temple car made by stone and it is an excellent work.

Thoothukudi.x: Thoothukudi, formerly Tuticorin, is a city in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. Thoothukudi is the headquarters of Thoothukudi District which is located at the southeastern part of Tamil Nadu. It is almost 580 km away from Chennai, about 261 km away from Tiruchirappalli and about 133 km away from Madurai.
Thoothukudi.icon: Tuticorin Thermal Power Station at Night 1 crop.jpg

sights.d: The church dates back to the 16th century. The basilica is dedicated to Lady of Snow a title given to St. Mary.
Built by the Dutch East India Company (VOC) the church dates back to 1750. The VOC monogram and the year 1750 (in Roman numerical) are displayed above the main entrance.

Toranagallu.x: Toranagallu is a village in Northern Karnataka.

Tiptur.x: Tiptur is a city in Tumkur District, Karnataka, India. Tiptur is known as Kalpataru Nadu.

Thirubuvanai.x: Thirubuvanai, a village at the outskirts of Pondicherry, home to Chola temples.

sights.d: A Vishnu temple and a storehouse of Chola architecture. It is believed to have been built by Parantaka I.

Tripura.x: Tripura, one of the seven north-eastern states of India, is one of the least explored regions of India by tourists, but it offers immense natural beauty and an intriguing cultural heritage. A mix of Bengali and tribal populations, Tripura is bordered by Bangladesh in the south, west, and north, Assam in the northeast, and Mizoram in the east.
Tripura.icon: Ujjayanta palace Tripura State Museum Agartala India.jpg

Tulu phrasebook.x: Tulu is a regional language spoken in coastal districts of Karnataka, i.e. Dakshina Kannada, Udupi and some areas of Kasaragod District . It is the 24th most populous Indian language according to the 2001 census of India.

Tumkur.x: Tumkur, officially known as Tumakuru, is in Karnataka state of India.

sights.d: Sri Siddaganaga Mutt is a main attraction of Tumkur, where around 8000 students are provided education, boarding and lodging free of cost.
Devaraayana Durga is a famous hill station and a religious place about 15 km from the City of Tumkur.
KaidaaLa has a famous Sri Chenna Keshava Swamy temple which dates back to the hoysalas.
Goravanahalli is one of the popular pilgrim centres located in the Koratagere taluk of Tumkur district.The temple here is dedicated to goddess Mahalakshmi.
Shri Kamakshi Sharada Temple managed by Shri Kodandashrama Mutt of Hebbur, is situated in Tumkur Taluk, Tumkur district of Karnataka.
Siddara Betta Sacred Place where 9000 siddaru (holy spiritual men) made meditation and worship of Lord Shiva, They got mooksha (freedom) from this eternal world.

Udaipur.x: Udaipur is the capital of the district of Mewar in Rajasthan, India. Udaipur is famous for its lakes, palaces, forts, temples, gardens, and romantic backdrops. It was the setting of many movies, including the 13th James Bond film, Octopussy.

sights.d: A complex of small and big palaces, museums and gardens encompassing a rich blend of Rajasthani, Mughal, Medieval, European and Chinese architecture established in 1559…
Located 150 m north of the palace in Indo-Aryan architectural style, the temple is dedicated to Lord Vishnu.
An artificial lake constructed by Maharana in north of Lake Pichola in 1678 and to the north-west of Udaipur.
An artificial fresh water lake, created in 1362 AD, named after the submerged Picholi village.
A rose garden laid out by Maharaja Sajjan Singh is near the palace on the east side of Lake Pichhola.
Built by Maharana Bhopal Singh. Saheliyon ki Bari means Garden of the Maids.
sights.img: Magical aura created by nature and architecture @ Garden of Maidens.jpg

sights.d: An old building built right on the waterfront of Lake Pichola at Gangori Ghat.
sights.img: 20191207 Gangaur Ghat and Bagore Ki Haveli, Udaipur 1524 7266.jpg

sights.d: The Ahar Cenotaphs are a group of royal cenotaphs in Ahar, about 2 km east of Udaipur.

Udhampur.x: Udhampur is the second-largest city in the Jammu Division of Jammu and Kashmir. It is 68 km from Jammu city.

sights.d: a spring considered to be the source of the Devika River.
Beautiful asharam and temple considered to be a very spiritual place and tourist attraction.

Ujjain.x: Ujjain is a city in the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh in India. It is home to the Mahakaleshwar Temple, one of the 12 Jyotirlingas of India, and famous for the Hindu pilgrimage Kumbh Mela, gathering hundreds of millions of pilgrims every 12 years.

sights.d: Like the Jantar Mantars in Delhi and Jaipur, this one is also built by Maharaja Jai Singh II in 1725.
One of the main attractions of Ujjain and one of the 12 Jyotirlingas. The Jyotirlingas are said to be the most sacred abodes of Shiva.
The worship of the eight Bhairavas is a part of Saivite tradition and the chief among them is Kal Bhairav, believed to have been built by King Bhadresen, on the banks of…
These caves are just above the bank of the Shipra near the temple of Gadkalika.
This distinctive monument glows like a small jewel in the surrounding lush landscape.
Situated on the banks of the Shipra, the island-like site immediately conjures up the natural beauty of ancient Ujjain which poets down the ages have waxed lyrical.

Ullal.x: Ullal is a city in Dakshina Kannada, a coastal region of the Indian province of Karnataka.

Unnao.x: Unnao is a city in Uttar Pradesh, and is known as the wellspring of freedom fighters and great writers.

sights.d: This Mandir is Lord Shiva Mandir. Here are also Ram Janki Mandir and Durga Mandir. Many devotees come here. After Diwali a very big Mela is held here.
A very spiritual temple.
Van Devi Mandir is a famous temple. It holds a fair, which is conducted every year by the villagers, is very famous and enjoyed by a lot of children.

Vadodara.x: Vadodara, also known as Baroda, is a city in Central Gujarat, India. It is named for the vaḍ trees that flourish in the area. It is known as the cultural capital of Gujarat.

sights.d: The museum displays Indian musical instruments, Mughal miniatures, sculptures, textiles and objects from Japan, Tibet, Nepal, Egypt.
Vadodara is quite serene. It was built by the Military and one can enjoy a pleasant hour in its premises.
The royal family of Baroda has a notable collection of his works. Apart from these, there are many art works of masters collected and commissioned by Maharaja Sayajirao.
The mausoleum contains the graves of Qutb-ud-din Muhammad Khan and his son Naurang Khan. It is an octagonal structure in the style of Mughal tombs.
sights.img: Hazira Maqbara during Emperor Akbar In Vadodara.JPG

sights.d: Another palatial building created by Sayajirao III in 1906 at a cost of 3 lakhs.
The cenotaph of the Maharajas of Baroda.
The imposing palace was built in the Indo-Saracenic tradition, with an eclectic mix of Indian, Islamic, and European elements by Maharaja Sayajirao III in 1890.
The world-famous Maharaja Sayajirao University has one of the largest campuses in Gujarat, full of beautiful historical buildings including Kala Bhavan, a former palace…

Vaikom.x: Vaikom is a town of 23,000 people (2011) in Kerala in India.

sights.d: Famous for Prathal (mid-day food offering by individual to others) and also Annathanam (served by the temple). Having this full fleged meal is very sacred too.
A centuries old Roman Syrian Catholic Church with ancient and rare interior architecture near the Vembanad Lake shore
Village backwater cruise, Visit different villages and village activities, ayurvedic treatment centre, Home stay with traditional Kerala food, night fishing etc.

Varanasi.x: Varanasi, also known as Banaras or Kashi, is a holy city at the banks of the Ganges River in Uttar Pradesh, India. Being the most sacred city in Hinduism and Jainism, and important in the history of Buddhism, Varanasi is India's most important pilgrimage destination. It was home to 1.2 million people as of 2011.

sights.d: Jantar Mantar literally means a combination of instruments and formulas (jantar = instrument and mantar = formula).
sights.img: Courtyard at Observatory of Man Singh.jpg

sights.d: the meeting of the five rivers.
The main cremation ghat; a must-see, but remain quiet and avoid taking photographs (scams are plentiful here; see the "Stay Safe" section).
Known as the 'main' ghat, this is the site of the large evening aarti ceremony. The ceremony starts right after the sunset and lasts for around 45 minutes.
The ghat was constructed by King Balwant Singh and played an important role during the Middle Ages.
A popular place for tourists, long-term students and researchers to stay, with many hotels, restaurants, and internet cafes nearby.
Lal Khan was the minister and commander of Balwant Singh (reign: 1740 – 70) the King of Varanasi (then Banaras).
A rather controversial mosque built during the rule of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb.

Varkala.x: Varkala is a town in the Indian state of Kerala, about 50 km north of Thiruvananthapuram and is home of the popular Papanasam Beach. Also, the Samadhi of Kerala's saint Sree Narayana Guru is in this town, and has become a place of pilgrimage.

sights.d: Varkala beach is as beautiful as, if not more beautiful than Kovalam beach. Laterite cliffs drop sharply into the sea, with a small strip of sandy beach at the base.

Valsad.x: Valsad is a city of 170,000 people (2011) in the Indian state Gujarat. It used to be called Bulsar and be the administrative capital of Valsad district. It's famous for its mango orchards and an increasingly popular destination with a nice beach and several temples.

sights.d: It is a hill with a small old fort and a temple. Mainly considered as northern most hill of western ghat.

Tufanganj.x: Tufanganj is a town in the Cooch Behar district of West Bengal.

sights.d: The ruins of an old fort built by Sukladwaja or Chilarai (1510–1571) of the Koch dynasty.
A larger brick-built fort with an earthen surrounding wall having lime and brickbat base, built around the same time as the smaller one.

Uttarpara.x: Uttarpara is an industrial town on the western bank of the Hooghly River, in the Hooghly district of West Bengal. Close to Kolkata, Uttarpara was a major automobile hub with India's first car factory, and although the city faced decline from the 1990s till the 2020s, it has been revived as a major manufacturing hub for metro vehicles in India.

sights.d: Possibly the only surviving terracotta temple in Uttarpara.
The oldest library in India and Asia. It contains some old and rare volumes of periodicals in both Bengali and English, including Digdarshan.
India's first car factory, and the manufacturing site of the iconic Hindustan Ambassador, once one of the most common car models plying on the city streets in India.

Ulhasnagar.x: Ulhasnagar is a suburb near Thane, in the North Konkan region of western Maharashtra. The town is known for its significant Sindhi refugees since the partition of India in 1947, and there have been calls by the Sindhis to rename it Sindhunagar.

sights.d: One of the most beautiful temples, dating back centuries and a must visit, which is maintained by the Birla Group.
A Sindhi religious and spiritual center known for its architecture and carvings.

Uluberia.x: Uluberia is a sleepy industrial town in the Howrah district of West Bengal, at the western bank of the Hooghly River. Uluberia is a delightful place for weekend visitors, with riverside views and a popular Kali temple.
Uluberia.banner: Ulubaria Kalibari Hari Mandir উলুবেড়িয়া কালীবাড়ি হরিমন্দির (cropped).jpg

sights.d: There's a huge car park opposite the main gate, although it is closed during festivals to facilitate the devotees.

Vapi.x: Vapi, an industrial town in South Gujarat, is a major transport hub serving the union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.
Vapi.icon: Jain Temple, Vapi GIDC, Vapi - panoramio.jpg

sights.d: A dam on the Daman Ganga River, the lifeline of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.

Vasco da Gama.x: Vasco da Gama is a port city in the west coast Indian state Goa. Vasco is Goa's most populous overgrown town and the adjoining Mormugao port are busy, dusty and mainly commercial centres.
Vasco da Gama.banner: Vasco da Gama, Goa WV banner.jpg

sights.d: This is a great place to see vintage aircraft like the Sealands, Doves, Alizes, Seahawks, Vampires and Hughes Helicopters, along with the relatively newer Sea Harriers…

Velankanni.x: Velankanni is a city in Tamil Nadu in India.

sights.n: Basilica of Our Lady of Health
sights.d: This Gothic church was raised to the status of a basilica in 1962 by Pope John XXIII. A beautiful museum is attached to the church.

Vellore.x: Vellore is a city of 505,000 people (2011) in Tamil Nadu, India. Visitors are drawn by its large 16th-century fort, which is known for its grand ramparts, wide moat and robust masonry. Apart from Fort tourism, Christian Medical College due to its esteemed position in the country, both as a medical college and a hospital, invites many students, medical practitioners, and patients from around the country.

sights.d: Dedicated to Sri Lakshmi Narayani or Maha Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth, in 2007.
This temple to Lord Shiva is a fine example of Vijayanagaram Architecture.
These are abandoned cliff top remains of forts built by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. This is recommended only for those with strength as it's accessible only via foot.
A large forested area near Javathu mountain. Amirthi Falls and Amirthi Zoo can be found here.
Temple dedicated to Lord Murugan with a huge statue of him also nearby
Murugan Temple on Palamathi Hill

Veraval.x: Veraval-Somnath is a city on the west coast of India in the Junagadh district in the state of Gujarat. The Somnath Temple in the Prabhas Kshetra, near Veraval, is the most sacred of the twelve Jyotirlings (lingas of light) of the God Shiva.

sights.d: It is one of the 12 Jyotirlinga temples dedicated to Lord Shiva. Three aartis (ritual) performed daily; at 7AM, at noon and at 7PM.

Vidarbha.x: Vidarbha, also known as Berar, is the easternmost region of Maharashtra, India. Although Maharashtra as a whole is considered a western state, geographically Vidarbha is very much at the centre of the country, on the Deccan Plateau.
Vidarbha.banner: WV banner Vidarbha Aerial view of Nagpur.jpg

Vijayawada.x: Vijayawada or Bezawada, the second-largest city in Andhra Pradesh, is the state's major commercial hub, on the upper banks of the Krishna River, opposite the state capital Amaravati. Famous for the Kanaka Durga Temple that attracts millions every year, Vijayawada is a part of the "Capital Region" (CR) of Andhra Pradesh, with almost all the amenities a traveller might need.

sights.d: This temple is on a hill (Indrakeeladri) overlooking the city and the River Krishna. One can either motor up the ghat road or take the steps on foot.
The first Gandhi Memorial with seven stupas in the country was constructed on this hill at a height of 500 ft (150 m).
Bhavani Island is on Krishna River close to the city. AP Tourism is converting this 133-acre (54-hectare) island into a tourist spot and a river-front resort.
Built across the river Krishna connecting this city with Amaravati, Prakasam Barrage has created a panoramic lake.
A group of 7th-century rock-cut caves dedicated to Shiva.
sights.img: Akkanna Madanna Rock cut Caves, Vijayawada city.jpg

sights.d: Said to have been excavated in the 5th century, these caves are reputed to be the first of their kind in South India.
A place for archaeology lovers, Victoria Museum has a carefully preserved collection of ancient sculptures, paintings, idols, weapons, cutlery, and inscriptions.
In 1925, Rf. Arlati, the Rector of St. Joseph's Orphanage at Gunadala, installed a statue of Our Lady.

Virudhaachalam.x: Virudhaachalam is a town in the Cuddalore to Salem Highway next to Neyveli in Tamil Nadu state in India. It is primarily a pilgrimage centre with an enormous Shiva temple, the Viruthagiriswarar temple, from which the name arose. The town is a good travel planning centre because it is linked to all the cities in Tamil Nadu by broad gauge railway network and good wide access roads.

sights.d: A Shiva temple.
Built for Lord Murugan. You can give grievance to God for fulfilling your wishes, and once your wishes get fulfilled you can withdraw it.
Built for Lord Muruga.
Palamalai Nathar Temple east 5 km near Veddeper Kovil.

Virudhunagar.x: Virudhunagar is a district of southern Tamil Nadu.

Visakhapatnam.x: Visakhapatnam, popularly known as Vizag (vigh-ZAG), is the largest city in Andhra Pradesh. It is primarily an industrial city, but also attracts tourists due to its unspoilt sandy beaches, well built and maintained parks, Buddhist sites and nearby scenic areas, such as Araku Valley. The city has a population of about 2 million.

sights.d: A lighthouse providing an aerial view of the port and the city.
sights.img: Main entrance of Dolphin's Nose Lighthouse,Yarada Hill, Visakhapatnam.jpg

sights.d: The ride to this hill offers a spectacular view of the sea. There is a park atop the hill, with a beautiful view of the city, the sea and Eastern Ghats merging into the…
A crafts village showcasing and preserving the old, including woodwork, jewellery, clothes and local crafts of rural India.
A summer residential palace of the royal family of Jeypore, and one of the most iconic historical buildings of the city.
A museum in a decommissioned submarine of the Indian Navy. This is the first of its kind in South Asia.
The first military aviation museum in India. It exhibits a decommissioned Russian Tupolev Tu-142 anti-submarine aircraft of the Indian Navy, the heaviest, fastest and…

Vrindavan.x: Vrindavan, also spelled Brindavan, is a holy town at the banks of the Yamuna River, in the Braj region of the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh.

sights.d: The best-known temple in Vrindavan, home to a Krishna idol known as Thakur-ji.
It resembles the Tajmahal, built with white marble. It is a unique temple in that you are prohibited from donating if you are a non-vegetarian.
Better known as the ISKCON Temple. A major draw for Hare Krishna (ISKCON) pilgrims to India, and uniquely among Vrindavan's temples well equipped to deal with foreign…
The temple was constructed in 2012. There are fantastic light shows and designs. The light show closes at 7:30PM in the winter days, and at 8PM in the summer.
A very well-known ancient temple of Vrindavan, founded by Shri Hith Harivansh Mahaprabhu, Sri Radhavallabh Lal's idol resemble Sri Radha and Sri Krishna to be embodied…
The single largest temple in Vrindavan, built in 1851 in a South Indian style, complete with intricate seven-story gopuram (gateway) at the entrance.

Walayar.x: Walayar is a small developing town, in the Ernakulam District of Kerala, India. It is near the border between the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu on NH 47 where the sales tax, motor vehicles check post, and excise check posts are. Due to the high traffic on this route (most of the goods import into Kerala happens through road and predominantly through this road), the place has also become notorious for the traffic jams.

Warangal.x: Warangal is in East Telangana in Southern India. Historically known as Orugallu and also Ekashila Nagaram (City carved in single stone). Warangal is part of a tertiary city including Kazipet and Hanamkonda cities.

sights.d: One of the oldest temples for Goddess Bhadrakali, believed to be built in 625 AD by King Pulakeshin II of Chalukya dynasty.
Renovated in 2004.
Built in the 18th century.
Built in the 3rd century.

Wazirpur.x: Wazirpur is a village in the Bharatpur Division of Rajasthan.

Virpur.x: Virpur is a village 53 km from Rajkot reached through highway NH-8b.

Vatakara.x: Vatakara, Badagara or Vadagara is a town in the Kozhikode District of the Malabar region, in the state of Kerala, India.

sights.d: Rock-cut caves, murals and carvings. 1500 years old. Very famous temple in Malabar side, associated with the famous Kerala Ballards (Vakkum Pattu) and with the heroic…
Established in 1864
Famous for the Dhwaja Prathishta
Scenic hill top ideal to watch the sunset.
The dam site is open for visitors from 8:30AM to 5:00PM.
Beautiful sunsets

Vidisha.x: Vidisha is a historic city in Madhya Pradesh, India. Known for its ancient temples, archaeological sites, and cultural heritage, Vidisha is a must-visit destination for history enthusiasts and travellers exploring central India. Located about 60 km northeast of Bhopal, Vidisha is often overshadowed by the nearby UNESCO World Heritage Site of Sanchi, but it holds its own as a treasure trove of ancient history and architecture.

Vizianagaram.x: Vizianagaram is a city 40 km (25 mi) north-northeast of Visakhapatnam in northern Andhra Pradesh.

sights.d: An early 18th-century square-shaped fort, built by Maharaja Vijaya Rama Raju in 1713. It has two main gates, of which the main entrance is elaborately decorated.
The iconic octagonal clock tower of Vizianagaram. Built in 1885, the tower was partly inspired by the Big Ben in London.
The central lake of Vizianagaram.
Despite being newer than the Vizianagaram Raj era, Ramanarayanam is one of the most-visited attractions in and around the city, attracting millions of pilgrims.

Yelagiri.x: Yelagiri (also spelt Elagiri on some signboards) is a town in Tamil Nadu, a state in the south of India. Yelagiri, at a height of 920 metres above sea level, stands majestically amidst four mountains. This is a hill station with a salubrious climate prevailing throughout the year so that winters do not keep visitors away.

sights.d: Yellagiri Hills. Fr. Guezou, who is the founder of this Don Bosco Center has come from France and has been helping the poor people for many years.

Yadgir.x: Yadgir, also known as Yadagiri, is a town in Karnataka. It is dotted with many historical monuments and has a majestic hill fort with three rounds of fortifications. There are three ancient temples, medieval mosques, tanks and wells on top of the hill.

sights.d: Stands on the top of a 100-meter (328 feet) tall monolith

Yadagirigutta.x: Yadagirigutta is a Hindu pilgrimage site near Bhongir in West Telangana. It is often called the "Tirupati of Telangana" for its spiritual significance.

sights.d: The hilltop Hindu town that draws pilgrims to the town. The temple is dedicated to the god Narasimha, an Avatar of Vishnu.
